records.title: Quad-Dominant Subdivision Topology, Pole Routing & Edge-Flow Discipline
records.summary: Rules for constructing quad-dominant Catmull-Clark subdivision surfaces and deforming meshes, routing 3-edge (N-pole) and 5-edge (E-pole) vertices onto low-curvature planes, and placing support holding loops.
intent_signals: fix pinching or lumpiness on a Subdivision Surface mesh
route edge loops and poles for clean quad topology
add holding support loops for sharp creases under subdivision
prepare deforming character or hero product quad topology

when_to_apply: The mesh uses a Catmull-Clark Subdivision Surface modifier for close-up hero rendering or smooth curved silhouettes.
The mesh will deform via skeletal armature skinning or morph targets (shape keys) where triangles and N-gons cause shading creases.
when_not_to_apply: The surface is a completely flat, non-deforming architectural wall or floor plane that will never be subdivided or bent.
The asset is a final triangulated low-polyLOD export where MikkTSpace tangents are already locked.

prerequisites: Object scale applied to (1.0, 1.0, 1.0) and duplicate vertices merged by distance.
principles: Catmull-Clark subdivision averages vertex positions across quad rings; triangles and N-gons on curved transitions interrupt continuous edge loops and produce visible specular pinching.

Vertices with 3 edges (N-poles) or 5 edges (E-poles) are mathematically unavoidable when redirecting edge flow, but must be shifted at least one quad loop inset from sharp ridges onto flatter regions.
Vertices with 6 or more edges (high-valence stars) cause radiating shading ripples under subdivision and should be split into quad grids.
Support holding loops control crease tightness more predictably across FBX/glTF interchange than Blender-specific Mean Edge Crease weights.

workflow_steps: Establish primary silhouette loops and boundary perimeter loops before adding interior grid subdivisions.
Place parallel holding loops (via Loop Cut or a 2-segment Profile=1.0 Bevel modifier) on both sides of structural creases.
Inspect curved regions with a high-gloss zebra or studio MatCap and slide 3-edge and 5-edge poles away from silhouette crests onto planar regions.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Modifiers -> Generate -> Subdivision Surface (Catmull-Clark); Edit Mode -> Loop Cut (Ctrl+R) and Edge Slide (G, G); Viewport Shading -> MatCap.

observable_checks.check: Select vertices by trait or inspect curved ridges for 6+ edge star poles or N-gons.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Zero 6+ valence poles on curved surfaces and zero N-gons crossing curved borders.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Radiating star pinching visible under glossy MatCap reflection lines.

observable_checks.check: Compare quad aspect ratios across primary curved surfaces.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Quads remain near-square (aspect ratio < 4:1) across deforming or curved zones.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Elongated sliver quads cause stretched highlights and uneven subdivision density.

observable_checks.check: Verify Subdivision Surface viewport and render levels against scene triangle budget.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Subdivision levels are <= 2 (or 3 for macro close-ups) with each level multiplying quad count by 4x.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Subdivision level >= 4 explodes single-prop polygon count into millions of triangles.

creative_affordances: Wider spacing between holding loops yields soft, organic elastomeric or Cushion-like transitions; tighter spacing produces crisp machined metal edges.
Concentric anatomical loops around eyes, mouth, and joints allow natural skin compression and stretching without texture swim.
known_limits: Enforcing 100% quads on flat, non-subdivided hard-surface end-caps wastes triangles and complicates boolean cutouts unnecessarily.
Blender Edge Crease values do not transfer cleanly to standard glTF 2.0 unless the Subdivision Surface modifier is applied prior to export.

claims.statement: Each level of Catmull-Clark subdivision splits every quad into 4 quads and converts any triangle or N-gon into quads meeting at an extraordinary pole vertex.
claims.scope: Blender Subdivision Surface modifier across all supported Blender versions.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Deterministic mathematical property of Catmull-Clark subdivision.

claims.statement: Placing 3-edge or 5-edge poles directly on a curved crease or silhouette ridge interrupts curvature continuity and creates visible specular pinching.
claims.scope: Curved subdivision surfaces and specular materials.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Planar N-gons surrounded by a flat coplanar quad inset loop can subdivide without visible pinching.

records.title: Mesh Manifold Integrity, Outward Normals & Applied Scale Hygiene
records.summary: Foundational mesh hygiene invariants requiring applied unit scale (1,1,1), consistent outward face orientation, merged coincident vertices, and manifold closed volumes before modifiers, UV unwrapping, baking, rigging, or glTF export.
intent_signals: bevel or UV unwrap is stretched and uneven across axes
faces look inside-out, invisible, or dark in Three.js and Blender
check mesh for non-manifold edges, flipped normals, and unapplied scale
clean up imported CAD or FBX mesh geometry before texturing

when_to_apply: Before running Bevel, Solidify, Boolean, UV Unwrap, Armature skinning, physics simulation, or glTF/GLB export on any mesh.
When diagnosing unexplained shading black spots, uneven bevels, or inside-out backfaces in web viewers.
when_not_to_apply: When an object's non-uniform scale is intentionally animated via keyframes and no local-space bevel/unwrap modifier is stacked on top.
Intentional single-sided alpha foliage cards or open ground planes where a closed manifold volume is not expected.

prerequisites: Mesh object exists in Object Mode without locked transform channels.
principles: Mesh modifiers and UV unwrappers operate in local object space; if Object Scale is non-uniform (e.g., 1.0, 0.2, 3.5) or negative, bevel widths, solidify thicknesses, and UV islands distort proportionally.
Negative scale on any axis (-1.0) inverts the winding order of polygon vertices on export, causing backface culling to hide exterior surfaces in Three.js and game engines.
Consistent outward face normals are mandatory for refraction IOR calculations, Boolean inside/outside classification, and tangent-space normal map baking.
Zero-area faces, loose vertices, and interior faces trapped inside an edge shared by 3+ faces break manifold integrity and cause subdivision spikes.

workflow_steps: In Object Mode, select all meshes and run Object -> Apply -> Scale (or Rotation & Scale) so scale reads (1.000, 1.000, 1.000).
Enable Viewport Overlays -> Face Orientation to verify all exterior surfaces render blue (outward) and zero exterior surfaces render red (flipped).
In Edit Mode, select all (A), run Mesh -> Merge -> By Distance (0.0001 m), then Mesh -> Normals -> Recalculate Outside (Shift+N), and Select By Trait -> Non-Manifold to inspect unintended holes.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Object Mode -> Ctrl+A (Apply Scale); Edit Mode -> M (Merge by Distance), Shift+N (Recalculate Outside), Select -> Select All by Trait -> Non Manifold.

observable_checks.check: Inspect Transform Scale X, Y, Z in the N-panel for all mesh and armature objects.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Scale is exactly (1.000, 1.000, 1.000) with zero negative axes.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Non-unit or negative scale values present before modifier evaluation or export.

observable_checks.check: Enable Face Orientation overlay in the 3D Viewport.
observable_checks.pass_condition: 100% of visible exterior surfaces are blue (front-facing).
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Red (back-facing) patches appear on exterior surfaces.

observable_checks.check: Run Merge by Distance (0.0001m) and Select All by Trait -> Interior Faces.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Zero duplicate vertices and zero internal partitions shared by 3+ faces.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Coincident vertices clamp bevels to zero or interior faces pinch subdivision surfaces.

creative_affordances: Guaranteed 1:1 metric scale ensures procedural wear masks, bevel widths (in mm), and subsurface scattering radii transfer predictably across every asset in a scene.
Clean manifold volumes allow effortless Boolean slicing and 3D printing/simulation reuse.
known_limits: Applying scale on multi-user linked mesh data requires making the mesh single-user or applying scale consistently across all instances.
Open single-sided shells (e.g., cloth capes, foliage cards) will always highlight boundary edges under Select Non-Manifold; boundary edges on open sheets are acceptable if intentional.

claims.statement: Blender evaluates mesh modifiers and UV unwrapping in local object coordinates before object-level scale transforms are applied, causing non-uniform object scale to skew bevels and UVs.
claims.scope: All Blender mesh modifiers and UV operators.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Applies to Blender 3.0+, 3.6 LTS, 4.2 LTS, and 5.1+.

claims.statement: An odd number of negative scale axes reverses triangle vertex winding order, causing inverted face normals in downstream glTF viewers.
claims.scope: glTF 2.0 export and WebGL backface culling.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Defined in Khronos glTF 2.0 specification (counter-clockwise front-face winding).

records.title: Boolean Cutout Shading Cleanup, Custom Split Normals & Smooth by Angle
records.summary: Techniques for preventing diagonal shading streaks, pinched normals, and bevel overlap spikes after Boolean operations on flat and curved surfaces across Blender 3.6 LTS and 4.1+/4.2 LTS.
intent_signals: fix dark diagonal shading gradients after Boolean difference
how to replace Auto Smooth in Blender 4.1 and 4.2 LTS
clean up Boolean cutouts on a curved cylinder without pinching
stop Bevel modifier from clamping or spiking after a Boolean cut

when_to_apply: After cutting holes, vents, or recesses into flat or curved meshes using Boolean modifiers or destructive knife/boolean tools.
When migrating shading setups from Blender 3.6 LTS (Mesh Auto Smooth checkbox) to Blender 4.1+/4.2 LTS/5.1+ (Smooth by Angle modifier).
when_not_to_apply: Purely organic sculpted characters that do not use sharp mechanical creases or boolean cutouts.

prerequisites: Boolean operand meshes are manifold with applied scale (1,1,1) and outward normals.
principles: Default smooth shading averages vertex normals equally across all adjacent faces, causing small bevel faces to pull the normals of large flat faces and produce dark gradients.

Weighted Normal (Face Area weight) forces large flat faces to dominate vertex normals so shading stays planar across N-gons and triangles, provided the surrounding bevel has at least 1 segment and Keep Sharp is enabled.

On curved cylinders, boolean cuts must land on existing longitudinal cylinder segments (or inside an inset support loop) so the surrounding curved normal interpolation is isolated from the cut perimeter.

In Blender 4.1+, the legacy Mesh Data -> Normals -> Auto Smooth property was removed and replaced by the Smooth by Angle modifier (Geometry Nodes group), which must sit before or integrate with Weighted Normal.

workflow_steps: Match the segment count of cylindrical boolean cutters to the host cylinder's vertical edge density so vertices align rather than creating sub-millimeter slivers.
Insert a Weld modifier (Distance = 0.0001 m) after Boolean if nearly coincident vertices cause the subsequent Bevel modifier's Clamp Overlap to stall.

Add a Bevel modifier (Limit Method = Angle ~30 deg, Segments >= 1, Clamp Overlap = True) followed by Smooth by Angle (Blender 4.1+) and Weighted Normal (Weight = 50-100, Keep Sharp = True) at the very end of the modifier stack.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Modifiers -> Generate -> Boolean (Exact), Weld, Bevel; Modifiers -> Normals -> Smooth by Angle (4.1+) and Weighted Normal.

observable_checks.check: Orbit viewport with a high-contrast linear stripe/zebra MatCap across boolean-cut planar faces.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Reflection stripes remain straight and parallel across the flat face right up to the bevel edge.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Reflection lines bend or warp toward boolean corners.

observable_checks.check: Verify that the Bevel modifier visibly bevels edges to the specified millimeter width.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Bevel width matches target parameter without collapsing to zero width.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Single stray vertex pair near a boolean corner causes Clamp Overlap to freeze the entire object's bevel.

observable_checks.check: Verify normal smoothing setup matches the active Blender version.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Blender 3.6 LTS uses Mesh Auto Smooth + Weighted Normal (Keep Sharp); Blender 4.2 LTS / 5.1+ uses Smooth by Angle modifier or Bevel Harden Normals + Weighted Normal.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Instructions reference the removed `mesh.use_auto_smooth` property on Blender 4.2 LTS.

creative_affordances: Allows rapid iteration on complex vents, grip cutouts, and industrial housings without manual quad-rebuilding of every flat face.
Produces crisp specular edge highlights that read clearly even at mid-poly real-time budgets.
known_limits: Weighted Normals cannot hide shading pinches on curved surfaces if a boolean cut interrupts curved edge flow without support loops or sufficient cylinder segments.

Custom split normals must be preserved on export (glTF 2.0 exports custom normals automatically when Export Normals is enabled, but subsequent runtime geometry recalculation in Three.js `computeVertexNormals()` will overwrite them!).

claims.statement: Blender 4.1 removed the mesh-level Auto Smooth checkbox (`use_auto_smooth`) and replaced it with the modifier-based Smooth by Angle operator and node group.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Blender 3.6 LTS still uses the legacy Mesh Data -> Normals -> Auto Smooth checkbox.

source_refs.locator: Blender 4.1 Release Notes — Modeling & Normals (Auto Smooth Replacement)

claims.statement: Weighting vertex normals by face area aligns shared vertex normals with large planar polygons, transferring all normal curvature onto the narrow bevel chamfers.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Requires at least one bevel segment between orthogonal faces.

source_refs.locator: Boolean, Bevel, Smooth by Angle & Weighted Normal Modifiers

records.title: Non-Destructive Hard-Surface Modifier Stack Ordering & Evaluation Rules
records.summary: Canonical ordering rules for stacking Mirror, Solidify, Boolean, Weld, Bevel, Subdivision/Triangulate, and Weighted Normal modifiers so hard-surface models remain editable without destructive geometry application.
intent_signals: what order should I stack Mirror, Boolean, Bevel, and Weighted Normal modifiers
build a non-destructive hard-surface workflow in Blender
prevent seam creases down the center of a Mirror modifier
stack multiple Bevel modifiers by vertex group or angle

when_to_apply: Designing manufactured products, consumer electronics, vehicles, weapons, or architectural hardware that require iterative design changes.
Auditing modifier stacks before UV unwrapping or baking.
when_not_to_apply: Final low-poly export stage when modifiers must be applied or evaluated by the glTF exporter (`Export Apply Modifiers`).

prerequisites: Object origin placed on the symmetry plane and object scale applied to (1.0, 1.0, 1.0).
principles: Blender evaluates modifiers strictly top-to-bottom; placing Subdivision or Weighted Normal above a Boolean or Bevel modifier invalidates custom normals and exponentially slows boolean solver intersections.
Mirror with Merge and Bisect/Clipping enabled must precede Bevel so edges crossing the symmetry centerline merge seamlessly rather than being beveled as an open seam.

Hierarchical beveling (a larger primary bevel on structural edges via Vertex Group/Bevel Weight followed by a finer 30-degree angle-limited secondary bevel) creates realistic multi-tier manufactured chamfers.
Weighted Normal (or Smooth by Angle) must always sit at the bottom of the non-deforming modeling stack because any subsequent topology change destroys custom split normals.

workflow_steps: Order the stack top-to-bottom: (1) Mirror (Merge=0.001m, Clipping=True) -> (2) Solidify (Even Thickness=True, if sheet metal/shell) -> (3) Boolean (Exact solver) -> (4) Weld (0.0001m) -> (5) Primary/Secondary Bevel (Clamp Overlap=True, Miter Outer=Arc) -> (6) Weighted Normal (Keep Sharp=True).
Set Bevel Miter Outer to 'Arc' instead of 'Sharp' to prevent three-way corner triangles and improve UV/shading continuity.
Keep boolean cutter objects in a dedicated 'Cutters' collection with Viewport Display = Wire/Bounds and Render visibility disabled.

recommended_parameters.stack_order: Mirror -> Solidify -> Boolean -> Weld -> Bevel -> WeightedNormal

implementation_guidance.blender_context: Properties -> Modifiers tab; Object Properties -> Viewport Display -> Display As: Wire (for Boolean cutters).

observable_checks.check: Inspect the modifier stack order from top to bottom.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Weighted Normal (and Triangulate with Keep Normals, if baking) is at the bottom of the modeling stack after all topology-changing modifiers.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Boolean or Bevel placed below Weighted Normal discards custom split normals and triggers a Blender modifier warning.

observable_checks.check: Inspect the symmetry plane where the Mirror modifier meets.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Zero visible seam or unwanted bevel groove along the mirror centerline.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Bevel placed above Mirror chamfers the open symmetry boundary.

observable_checks.check: Verify visibility flags on the Boolean cutters collection in the Outliner.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Cutters collection has Disable in Viewports / Disable in Renders (camera icon) unchecked for final output and excluded from glTF export.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Wireframe cutter boxes render as solid geometry in Cycles or export as extra meshes in GLB.

creative_affordances: Non-destructive boolean cutters can be slid, scaled, or duplicated in real time while bevels and weighted normals update live in the viewport.
Arc outer miters on bevels generate clean quad corner patches that accept procedural edge-wear curvature masks.
known_limits: Stacking 10+ Exact-solver Boolean modifiers on dense meshes degrades viewport playback speed; convert stable upstream cutters to applied base mesh checkpoints on a duplicate collection when needed.
UV unwrapping requires real geometry; live procedural boolean faces only get auto-generated UVs from cutter materials until modifiers are applied for final UV packing.

claims.statement: Blender evaluates the object modifier stack sequentially from top to bottom; any modifier that adds or splits vertices invalidates custom normals computed by an earlier modifier.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Consistent across Blender 3.0+, 3.6 LTS, 4.2 LTS, and 5.1+.

claims.statement: Setting Bevel Miter Outer to Arc replaces pinch-prone 3-way corner poles with spread quad/arc fillets.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Supported in Blender 3.0+ through 5.1+.

records.title: Organic High-Poly Sculpting to Clean Quad Retopology & Detail Transfer
records.summary: Workflow for transitioning from dynamic-topology or voxel-remeshed high-poly organic sculpts to animation-ready low/mid-poly quad retopology with Shrinkwrap projection and Multiresolution / normal-map detail transfer.
intent_signals: retopologize a high-poly sculpt for animation or web GLB export
transfer sculpted details to a low-poly mesh with Shrinkwrap and Multires
when to use Voxel Remesh vs Dyntopo vs Multiresolution in Blender sculpting
reduce a 2-million-polygon sculpt into a clean quad mesh

when_to_apply: Creating organic characters, creatures, footwear uppers, cushions, rocks, or botanical assets sculpted at high polygon counts.
Converting a dense scan or voxel-remeshed sculpt into an UV-unwrappable, riggable, or web-exportable mesh.
when_not_to_apply: Geometric architectural walls or rectilinear mechanical parts that can be box-modeled directly at low polycount.

prerequisites: High-poly reference sculpt silhouette is locked so retopology does not have to be redone after major form changes.
principles: Voxel Remesh (Ctrl+R in Sculpt Mode) generates uniform isotropic grids ideal for primary/secondary form blocking, but destroys UV maps, vertex groups, and animation edge flow.
Automatic quad remeshing (Quadriflow) is suitable for static rocks or props, whereas deforming faces and limbs require guided quad loops around concentric muscle/joint rings.

Projecting a clean quad base mesh onto the frozen high-poly sculpt via a Multiresolution modifier + Shrinkwrap modifier captures micro-surface detail while preserving clean low-level subdivision topology and UVs.
For real-time web/game delivery, high-frequency Multiresolution/sculpt detail is baked into a tangent-space normal map and ambient occlusion map on the Level 0/1 quad mesh.

workflow_steps: Block primary and secondary forms using Voxel Remesh; freeze the high-poly sculpt as `<asset>_high` before starting retopology.
Construct the low-poly quad cage `<asset>_low` using surface snapping (Snap to Face Project) and Shrinkwrap modifier targeting `<asset>_high`, placing concentric loops around eyes, mouth, and joints.

Unwrap `<asset>_low` UVs cleanly, then bake Normal, AO, and Curvature maps from `<asset>_high` to `<asset>_low` (or subdivide with Multiresolution + Shrinkwrap Apply Base for offline Cycles rendering).
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Sculpt Mode -> Remesh; Edit Mode -> Snapping (Face Project) + Retopology Overlay (Blender 4.0+); Modifiers -> Multiresolution & Shrinkwrap.

observable_checks.check: Toggle visibility between `<asset>_high` and `<asset>_low` from the primary camera angle.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Outer silhouette contour of `<asset>_low` matches `<asset>_high` without obvious facet stepping.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Normal maps cannot fake missing silhouette geometry along grazing edges.

observable_checks.check: Inspect edge loops at elbows, knees, fingers, eyelids, and lips on deforming meshes.
observable_checks.pass_condition: At least 3 parallel quad loops span every bending joint and concentric loops surround facial orifices.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Spiral remesher loops cross joints diagonally and collapse volume during bending.

observable_checks.check: Verify that the multi-million-triangle `<asset>_high` sculpt is disabled for export.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Only `<asset>_low` with baked textures is included in the exported GLB.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Exporting `<asset>_high` produces a 100+ MB GLB that crashes web viewers.

creative_affordances: Decouples expressive sculptural freedom during concepting from strict technical topology and UV constraints.
Allows a single retopologized base mesh to serve both a 4K Multiresolution Cycles portrait and a 15k-triangle mobile GLB.
known_limits: Voxel Remesh cannot be used after UVs or shape keys are authored without losing them.
Extreme overhang cavities (deep ears, nostrils, between fingers) can cause Shrinkwrap projection spikes unless masked or projected with a distance limit.

claims.statement: Blender's Voxel Remesher rebuilds the mesh surface from a volumetric signed-distance grid, discarding existing UV maps, vertex groups, and shape keys.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Documented in Blender Manual Sculpting -> Remesh.

claims.statement: Blender 4.0+ provides a built-in Retopology viewport overlay that renders the active edit-mode mesh with a customizable depth offset in front of the reference sculpt.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: In Blender 3.6 LTS, use Object Properties -> Viewport Display -> In Front.

blender_versions.version_notes: Blender 4.0+ adds the dedicated Retopology viewport shading overlay. Verified against Blender 4.5.15 LTS and 5.2.3 LTS documentation (live runtime: Not Run).

records.title: Physical Bevel Minimums, Panel Seam Gaps & Industrial Readability
records.summary: Industrial design rules for sizing edge bevels and panel seams in physical millimeters so specular catchlights and shadow gaps remain legible at camera distance without sub-pixel aliasing.
intent_signals: how wide should bevels and panel gaps be on a product model
edges look razor sharp and CGI fake in product render
panel lines shimmer or disappear at camera distance
add realistic manufactured tolerances and seams to a product hero

when_to_apply: Modeling or auditing consumer electronics, footwear, watches, automotive parts, furniture, or sci-fi props for hero rendering or web viewers.
when_not_to_apply: Distant background buildings where sub-centimeter bevels are smaller than 0.5 screen pixels.

prerequisites: Scene unit scale set to Metric 1.0 (1 BU = 1 meter) and object scale applied.
principles: Zero-radius mathematical 90-degree edges do not exist on manufactured objects and cannot catch specular area-light reflections along their silhouette.
To prevent sub-pixel specular aliasing (shimmering) at standard HD/4K camera distances, primary housing bevels should measure 0.5 mm to 3.0 mm and micro-chamfers at least 0.15 mm to 0.4 mm.

Physical panel gaps (parting lines between housing shells) require an inward extruded recess depth of >= 1.5x the gap width (e.g., 0.5 mm wide x 0.8 mm deep) so ambient occlusion and grazing light form a crisp dark shadow line.
Hierarchy of detail (70% primary clean read / 20% secondary parting lines & fasteners / 10% tertiary micro-knurling or decals) prevents visual noise.

workflow_steps: Establish a 3-tier bevel hierarchy: Tier 1 outer silhouette fillets (2.0-5.0 mm), Tier 2 housing breaks (0.5-1.5 mm), and Tier 3 machined chamfers (0.2-0.4 mm).
Construct parting lines by splitting or insetting panel borders by 0.3-0.8 mm, extruding inward by 0.6-1.5 mm, and beveling the outer lip so light catches one rim of the gap.
For real-time GLB targets under strict triangle budgets, bake Tier 3 micro-fasteners and shallow vents into the normal/AO map while keeping Tier 1-2 silhouette bevels in geometry.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Scene Properties -> Units -> Length: Millimeters (or Meters); Bevel Modifier -> Offset (Width) in mm.

observable_checks.check: Inspect hero product edges under studio key and rim lighting.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Every visible structural corner exhibits a continuous specular highlight ribbon.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Unbeveled 90-degree edges appear dead and invisible where two dark faces meet.

observable_checks.check: Inspect parting lines between manufactured shells at final render resolution.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Parting lines have an occluded dark interior trough and a bright catchlight on the opposing lip.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Shallow V-grooves reflect bright light from their bottom face instead of reading as a physical gap.

observable_checks.check: Evaluate visual rest areas vs. detail clusters across the prop.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Approximately 70% rest surfaces, 20% secondary seams, 10% dense focal hardware.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Uniform greeble density across 100% of the surface destroys focal hierarchy.

creative_affordances: Slightly exaggerating micro-bevels by 1.2x-1.5x over CAD engineering drawings makes small products read as tactile and premium on 1080p/2K web screens.
Contrasting matte blasted recesses inside panel grooves against satin or gloss outer shells amplifies form definition.
known_limits: Geometry panel gaps add 4-6 quad loops per seam; on mobile web targets (<50k tris), secondary panel seams should be baked into tangent-space normal and AO maps.

claims.statement: Specular BRDF reflections only occur where surface normals orient the half-vector toward a light source; unbeveled 90-degree polygon edges have zero surface area at intermediate normal angles and therefore produce zero edge catchlights.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Cycles offers a shader-only Bevel node for offline renders, but it does not export to glTF 2.0.

claims.statement: Blender's Shader Editor Bevel node is a Cycles-only raytracing shader effect that is ignored by EEVEE and the glTF 2.0 exporter unless baked into a normal map.
claims.scope: Blender Cycles vs. EEVEE and glTF 2.0 export.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Verified in Blender Manual Shader Nodes -> Input -> Bevel.

records.title: Geometry Nodes Fields Evaluation, Attribute Domains & UV/Shader Persistence
records.summary: Core architecture of Blender Geometry Nodes Fields, attribute domain interpolation (Point, Edge, Face, Face Corner, Instance), and explicit `Store Named Attribute` contracts required to pass UVs and custom data to shaders and glTF exports.
intent_signals: how do I pass Geometry Nodes attributes or UVs to a material shader
textures disappear on procedural Curve to Mesh or Realize Instances
store UVMap on Face Corner domain in Geometry Nodes
understand Geometry Nodes field evaluation and Capture Attribute

when_to_apply: Building any Geometry Nodes procedural mesh generator, curve sweep (`Curve to Mesh`), or attribute-driven material variation.
Preparing a Geometry Nodes asset for textured rendering or glTF/GLB export.
when_not_to_apply: Static hand-modeled meshes that do not use Geometry Nodes modifiers.

prerequisites: Blender 3.0+ Fields architecture (3.6 LTS or 4.2 LTS recommended for full `Store Named Attribute` workflow).
principles: A Field in Geometry Nodes is a deferred function Recipe (dashed link) that is only evaluated when plugged into a Geometry-consuming operation node (solid link) in the context of that node's target attribute domain.

UV coordinates MUST be stored on the `Face Corner` domain as a `2D Vector` named `UVMap` (using `Store Named Attribute`); storing UVs on the `Point` (vertex) domain prevents UV splits at seams and causes wrap-around texture smearing.
`Capture Attribute` freezes a field's value on a specific geometry domain before topology-changing operations (such as `Curve to Mesh`, `Extrude Mesh`, or `Subdivide Mesh`) alter indices or normals.

Shaders access Geometry Nodes attributes via the Shader Editor `Attribute` node (`Type: Geometry` for Point/Face/Face Corner attributes on meshes, or `Type: Instancer` for attributes stored on the `Instance` domain).

workflow_steps: For `Curve to Mesh` generators, capture `Spline Parameter -> Factor` on the curve (`Capture Attribute`, Float, Point domain) for U and profile curve `Spline Parameter -> Factor` for V, combine into a Vector (`Combine XYZ`), and write to `Store Named Attribute` (`2D Vector`, `Face Corner`, Name = `UVMap`).
Expose all user-tunable parameters on the `Group Input` interface with explicit Min, Max, and Default values and descriptive socket names.
In the Shader Editor, add `Input -> Attribute` (`Name: UVMap`, `Type: Geometry`) and wire its `Vector` output into `Image Texture` nodes to guarantee consistent rendering in both Cycles and EEVEE.

records.title: Procedural Collection Instancing vs. Realize Instances Memory & Export Tradeoffs
records.summary: Memory, draw-call, and export rules governing `Instance on Points` vs. `Realize Instances`, preventing accidental multi-gigabyte mesh explosions while ensuring correct glTF/Three.js instance or merged-mesh output.
intent_signals: when should I use Realize Instances in Geometry Nodes
Blender runs out of memory or freezes when scattering trees or rocks
export Geometry Nodes instances to GLB or Three.js InstancedMesh
difference between unique mesh triangles and instanced triangles

when_to_apply: Scattering repeated props, foliage, architectural modules, or fasteners via Geometry Nodes (`Instance on Points`) or Collection Instances.
Auditing scene memory and polycount budgets in `polycount-budget-checker` and `mobile-glb-budget`.
when_not_to_apply: Single unique hero mesh with zero repeated components.

prerequisites: Base instance meshes have applied scale (1,1,1) and clean origin placement.
principles: An unrealized instance stores only a 4x4 transformation matrix (64 bytes) referencing shared mesh data; realizing 10,000 instances of a 20,000-triangle tree copies 200,000,000 unique triangles into RAM/VRAM.

Use `Realize Instances` ONLY when vertices of individual instances must be deformed differently downstream (e.g., bending instances along a curve or running a boolean across them) or when intentionally merging ultra-low-poly micro-parts into a single static draw call.

On `Collection Info`, enabling `Separate Children` + `Reset Children` + `Pick Instance` on `Instance on Points` randomly selects individual collection assets at the target point positions without double-applying collection world offsets.

When exporting to GLB, unrealized instances export as multiple glTF nodes referencing a single shared `mesh` index (keeping `.glb` file size tiny, though web engines should batch high node counts into `THREE.InstancedMesh`).

workflow_steps: Place source scatter assets in a dedicated collection with origins at the base contact point and enable `Separate Children` and `Reset Children` on `Collection Info`.
Enable `Pick Instance` on `Instance on Points` so each point instances one child rather than the entire collection at once.
Audit both `Unique Triangles` (VRAM/file size driver) and `Total Evaluated Scene Triangles` (rasterization vertex load) in `polycount-budget-checker`.

observable_checks.pass_condition: Both unique geometry memory and total rasterized triangles are reported.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Counting only unique triangles hides a 50-million-triangle rasterization bottleneck on mobile GPUs.

creative_affordances: Allows lush forests, brick walls, and stadium seating in Cycles/EEVEE using minimal RAM.
Nested instancing (instancing modular wall assemblies that themselves instance rivets/windows) scales to massive environments.

Realizing instances merges objects into one mesh and strips per-object transform hierarchy.

records.title: Poisson Disk Point Distribution, Slope/Altitude Masking & Orientation Alignment
records.summary: Mathematical and procedural patterns for natural, non-overlapping surface scattering using Poisson Disk minimum-distance distribution, surface-normal dot-product slope filtering, and stable Euler-to-vector orientation alignment.
intent_signals: stop scattered rocks, trees, or droplets from intersecting each other
scatter grass only on flat ground and not on steep cliffs
align scattered instances to surface normal without twisting
use Distribute Points on Faces Poisson Disk in Geometry Nodes

when_to_apply: Scattering vegetation, rocks, debris, condensation water droplets, or architectural props across terrain or product surfaces.
when_not_to_apply: Regular deterministic grid arrays (use Mesh Grid or Curve Resample instead of Poisson Disk).

prerequisites: Emitter surface has applied unit scale (1,1,1) and outward face normals.
principles: `Distribute Points on Faces` in `Random` mode places points independently and causes severe mesh overlaps; `Poisson Disk` mode enforces a hard minimum Euclidean `Distance Min` radius (blue-noise distribution) that prevents bounding-sphere collisions.

Taking the `Dot Product` of the surface `Normal` vector with world up `(0, 0, 1)` yields `cos(theta)` (`1.0` on flat horizontal ground, `0.0` on vertical walls, `-1.0` on overhangs), providing a resolution-independent slope mask.

Vertical objects (trees, lampposts, architectural columns) should blend 70-100% toward world `+Z` `(0,0,1)` and only 0-30% toward the terrain normal, whereas ground-hugging moss, pebbles, and droplets align 100% of their local `+Z` to the surface `Normal`.
Hierarchical scattering (scattering large boulders with a large `Distance Min` first, then masking small pebbles/grass around them via `Geometry Proximity`) mimics natural ecological clustering.

workflow_steps: Set `Distribute Points on Faces` to `Poisson Disk`, set `Distance Min` to approximately 0.8x the base diameter of the scattered asset, and set `Density Max` to a bounded ceiling.

Compute `Vector Math (Dot Product)` between `Normal` and `(0, 0, 1)`, pass through a `Map Range` or `Compare (Greater Than)` node (e.g., `> 0.70` for slopes under ~45 degrees), and multiply with a 3D `Noise Texture` into `Density Factor`.

Orient instances using `Align Euler to Vector` (or `Align Rotation to Vector` in Blender 4.2+): align `Z` axis to `Normal` (or `Mix Vector` between `(0,0,1)` and `Normal`), then chain `Rotate Euler` (Local, `Z` axis, `Random Value 0..2*pi`) for yaw variation.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Geometry Node Editor -> Point -> Distribute Points on Faces (Poisson Disk); Utilities -> Rotation -> Align Rotation to Vector (4.2+) / Align Euler to Vector (3.6 LTS).

creative_affordances: Combining slope dot-product, world-Z altitude, and ambient occlusion/curvature into `Density Factor` creates believable snowlines, moss crevices, and shoreline transitions automatically.
Micro-droplet Poisson scattering on beverage bottles or sneakers adds instant studio macro realism.
known_limits: `Distribute Points on Faces` evaluates per mesh surface; if the emitter mesh is animated/deforming, surface area changes can cause points to pop unless evaluated on a static rest-position reference (`rest_position` attribute).

records.title: UV Seam Placement, Hard-Edge Splits, Texel Density & Mipmap Padding
records.summary: Rules for placing UV seams along occluded contours and sharp shading breaks (>=60 degrees), equalizing texel density (pixels per meter), aligning islands to pixel axes, and sizing UV padding margins to prevent mipmap bleeding.
intent_signals: where should I place UV seams on my 3D model
how much UV margin padding do I need for 2K or 4K textures
fix blurry textures or uneven texel density across meshes
prevent mipmap color bleeding along UV island borders

when_to_apply: Unwrapping any 3D mesh for image texturing, normal/AO baking, or glTF 2.0 export.
Auditing UV stretching and texture sharpness in `material-quality-checker`.
when_not_to_apply: Untextured meshes that rely strictly on uniform material scalar values or camera-projected triplanar shaders inside offline Cycles renders.

prerequisites: Object scale is applied to (1.0, 1.0, 1.0) before running Unwrap or Average Islands Scale.
principles: Every sharp shading edge (hard edge / seam where vertex normals split, typically >= 60 degrees) MUST also be a UV seam with separated UV islands when baking tangent-space normal maps; otherwise the MikkTSpace tangent discontinuity creates a permanent black/bright ridge.
On smooth organic surfaces, hide UV seams along natural anatomical or clothing boundaries (under arms, inner legs, hairline, underside of footwear soles) away from the primary camera view.

Mipmap downsampling halves texture resolution at each level; without adequate pixel margin between UV islands (`>= 8 px` at 1024x1024, `>= 16 px` at 2048x2048, `>= 32 px` at 4096x4096), background or adjacent island colors bleed across seams at medium camera distances.
Aligning straight structural edges of UV islands horizontally or vertically (U or V axis) eliminates diagonal staircase aliasing on panel lines and stripes.

workflow_steps: Select all sharp edges (`Select -> Select Sharp Edges`, Angle ~60 deg) plus occluded relief cuts to flatten cylinders/cones, and run `UV -> Mark Seam`.
Run `UV -> Unwrap` (`Angle Based` for organic forms; `Conformal` or `Minimum Stretch` in Blender 4.3+/5.1+ for hard-surface mechanical parts).

Enable `UV Stretch` overlay (`Angle` and `Area`) in the UV Editor, run `UV -> Average Islands Scale`, and `UV -> Pack Islands` with Margin set to `0.008` (16 px at 2048x2048) and `Rotate Method = Axis-aligned`.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: UV Editor -> Overlays -> Stretching (Angle/Area); UV -> Unwrap, Average Islands Scale, Pack Islands.

creative_affordances: Giving focal hero surfaces (watch dial, sneaker logo tongue, character face) 1.5x-2.0x higher texel density than hidden undersides maximizes perceived 4K crispness inside a 2K texture budget.
Rectifying cylindrical straps and trims into straight rectangular UV strips allows clean weave/stitching tiling.
known_limits: Over-splitting every 30-degree bevel into tiny disconnected 2-pixel UV islands wastes UV space on padding margins and degrades KTX2 compression; keep smooth bevel fillets attached to one adjacent planar island.

records.title: Single 0-1 UV Atlas Packing vs. Multi-Tile UDIM Workflows for Offline & glTF
records.summary: Architectural selection rules between single `0..1` UV atlases (mandatory for standard single-material glTF/GLB web delivery), trim sheets / tiling `KHR_texture_transform` UVs, and multi-tile `1001..100N` UDIM layouts (for offline Cycles VFX).
intent_signals: should I use UDIMs or a single 0-1 UV atlas
do UDIM textures export to GLB and Three.js
combine multiple materials into a single texture atlas to reduce draw calls
use trim sheets and KHR_texture_transform in glTF

when_to_apply: Planning UV and texture architecture before unwrapping or baking.
Optimizing multi-material assets into a single draw-call atlas for web GLB delivery.
when_not_to_apply: Untextured geometry.

prerequisites: Target delivery surface (offline Cycles render vs. real-time glTF/GLB web viewer) is confirmed.
principles: Core Khronos glTF 2.0 and Three.js `GLTFLoader` do NOT natively resolve multi-tile `1001, 1002...` UDIM texture sequences on a single material; coordinates outside `0..1` simply wrap (`REPEAT`) or clamp (`CLAMP_TO_EDGE`) the single bound texture.
For real-time web GLB assets, packing all components of a prop into one `0..1` UV atlas (with non-overlapping islands for baked maps) allows a single PBR material and 1 draw call per mesh.

When an asset uses both a tiling detail texture (e.g., carbon fiber weave via `Mapping` scale -> `KHR_texture_transform`) and a baked non-overlapping Ambient Occlusion / lightmap, glTF 2.0 supports two UV sets: `TEXCOORD_0` (first UV map) and `TEXCOORD_1` (second UV map).
UDIM tiles (`1001`, `1002`, etc.) should be reserved for offline Cycles/VFX hero assets where a single unified shader needs multiple 4K/8K texture tiles without splitting material assignments.

workflow_steps: If targeting glTF/GLB web delivery, pack all unique baked islands strictly inside the `[0.0, 1.0]` UV square on `UVMap` (`TEXCOORD_0`).

If combining tiling weave/grain with baked AO, keep `UVMap` (`TEXCOORD_0`) for primary PBR maps and create a second non-overlapping `UVMap_AO` (`TEXCOORD_1`) wired via `UV Map` node into the glTF Occlusion socket.
If converting an offline UDIM asset to GLB, either bake and repack the UDIM tiles into a single `0..1` atlas or split the UDIM tiles into separate material slots with `0..1`-normalized UV offsets.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: UV Editor -> Image -> UDIM Tiles; Object Data Properties -> UV Maps (`UVMap`, `UVMap_AO`).

observable_checks.pass_condition: At most 2 UV maps (`TEXCOORD_0` and `TEXCOORD_1`).
observable_checks.fail_indicator: 3+ UV maps or unreferenced leftover UV layers bloat vertex buffer bandwidth.

creative_affordances: Dual-UV workflows (`TEXCOORD_0` trim/tiling + `TEXCOORD_1` baked macro AO) deliver crisp close-up fabric/wood grain on mobile web using tiny 512px tiling maps plus a 1024px AO map.
UDIMs in offline Cycles allow cinematic close-ups on large characters or vehicles without managing dozens of duplicate shader node trees.

`KHR_texture_transform` applies scale/offset/rotation in 2D UV space; 3D object/box-projected textures cannot be exported to glTF without baking to 2D UVs.

records.title: Tangent-Space MikkTSpace Normal & Ambient Occlusion Baking Protocol
records.summary: Precision baking rules for transferring high-poly or procedural surface detail onto low-poly meshes in Cycles using MikkTSpace (+X +Y +Z OpenGL), fixed pre-bake triangulation, cage extrusion, and 16-bit Non-Color buffers.
intent_signals: bake high-poly sculpt or bevels to a low-poly normal map in Blender
fix wavy lines, skewed details, or ray misses in baked normal maps
should Blender normal maps use +Y OpenGL or -Y DirectX for glTF and Three.js
prevent 8-bit banding in smooth baked normal maps

when_to_apply: Baking high-poly sculpts, subdivision surfaces, bevels, or procedural bump/shader setups into tangent-space normal and ambient occlusion maps.
Diagnosing inverted normal lighting or seam discontinuities in `material-quality-checker` and `blender-troubleshooting`.
when_not_to_apply: Flat untextured meshes or unbaked high-poly offline renders.

prerequisites: Low-poly mesh has non-overlapping `0..1` UVs, applied scale (1,1,1), and UV seams along all sharp edges.
principles: MikkTSpace tangent calculation depends on the exact diagonal triangulation of every quad; if the low-poly mesh is baked as quads and triangulated differently on export, the tangent basis changes and produces X-shaped shading crosses.

Blender, Khronos glTF 2.0, and Three.js all standardize on **OpenGL right-handed tangent space (`+X, +Y, +Z`)**; DirectX normal maps (`-Y` inverted green channel) cause lights from above to illuminate the bottom of bumps unless the G channel is inverted (`1.0 - G`).

Target normal map image buffers must be created with `Color Space = Non-Color` and `32-bit Float` (saved as 16-bit PNG before optional KTX2 UASTC encoding) to prevent 8-bit quantization stepping on smooth curved surfaces.

When baking `Selected to Active`, a custom Cage (or small `Extrusion` distance with constrained `Max Ray Distance`) ensures rays cast smoothly across 90-degree corners without gaps or cross-part self-intersection.

workflow_steps: Add a `Triangulate` modifier (`Quad Method: Fixed` or `Shortest Diagonal`, `Keep Normals: True`) to the low-poly mesh BEFORE baking and keep that exact triangulation for glTF export.
Create the target Image Texture node (`32-bit Float: True`, `Color Space: Non-Color`), leave it selected and disconnected in the low-poly material's Shader Editor.

In Render Properties (`Render Engine: Cycles`), set `Bake Type: Normal`, `Space: Tangent`, Swizzle `+X, +Y, +Z`, enable `Selected to Active` with `Extrusion` (e.g., `0.005 m` - `0.02 m`) or a pushed Cage mesh, set `Margin: 16 px` (`Adjacent Faces`), and bake.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Render Properties (Cycles) -> Bake -> Normal (Tangent, +X +Y +Z), Selected to Active, Cage/Extrusion, Margin.

observable_checks.pass_condition: Identical triangle diagonals are used during baking and final export.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Quad diagonals flip on export, producing diagonal shading crosses across curved panels.

observable_checks.check: Inspect the green channel of the normal map or shine a top directional light on a recessed engraving.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Top edge of a convex bump is bright in the green channel (+Y up) and recessed top edges are shadowed under a top light.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Recessed grooves appear embossed (inverted -Y DirectX normal map).

observable_checks.check: Inspect the baked normal map image for flat `(0.5, 0.5, 1.0)` patches or cross-projected limb imprints.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Continuous normal detail across all islands with zero ray misses or self-intersection ghosts.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Extrusion distance was too small (ray misses High-Poly) or `Max Ray Distance` was `0.0` (infinite rays hit opposite sides of the model).

creative_affordances: Allows a 5,000-triangle real-time web prop to display the visual bevels, stitching, and fastener detail of a 2,000,000-triangle CAD/sculpt model.
Baking a Bent Normal or Ambient Occlusion map enriches cavity contact shadows under soft environment lighting.

Symmetric UV islands stacked directly on top of each other during baking will collide and corrupt the bake unless all duplicate islands except one are offset by `+1.0` in U outside the `0..1` square.

records.title: Principled BSDF v2 Energy Conservation, Dielectric vs. Conductor Albedo & Blender 4.0+ Socket Changes
records.summary: Physically based shading rules for Blender's Principled BSDF (including the Blender 4.0+ Principled BSDF v2 multi-scatter GGX overhaul), enforcing energy-conserving albedo bounds, binary metalness discipline, and accurate Coat/Sheen/Transmission parameterization.
intent_signals: what changed in Principled BSDF in Blender 4.0 and 4.2 LTS
why do white or black materials look blown out or flat in renders
set physically accurate PBR values for metal, plastic, glass, and fabric
audit Principled BSDF materials for energy conservation

when_to_apply: Authoring or auditing any PBR material in Blender (`lighting-material-plan` and `material-quality-checker`).
Migrating shader graphs between Blender 3.6 LTS (`Principled BSDF v1`) and Blender 4.0+/4.2 LTS/5.1+ (`Principled BSDF v2`).
when_not_to_apply: Deliberately non-photorealistic (NPR) cel-shaded `Shader to RGB` cartoon materials that do not target PBR or glTF.

prerequisites: Scene color management configured to a high-dynamic-range view transform (`AgX` or `Filmic`).
principles: No real-world diffuse surface reflects 100% or 0% of incident light; dielectric `Base Color` luminance must stay within `[0.04, 0.90]` linear (`~35..240` sRGB) so carbon black retains specular form and snow/paper does not blow out global illumination.

Pure materials are either **dielectrics (`Metallic = 0.0`)** with a ~4% Fresnel reflectance (`IOR = 1.5`, `Specular IOR Level = 0.5`) or **conductors (`Metallic = 1.0`)** with zero diffuse bounce and tinted specular reflectance (`Base Color` linear luminance `0.55..0.98`); intermediate metallic values (`0.2..0.8`) only occur on sub-texel dust/oxidation transitions.

Every real surface has micro-imperfections; keep `Roughness` within `[0.02, 0.98]` with spatial roughness variation so specular highlights neither vanish into infinitesimal pinpoints (`0.0`) nor flatten into chalk (`1.0`).

Blender 4.0+ **Principled BSDF v2** orders layers top-to-bottom (`Coat -> Emission -> Specular/Metallic -> Diffuse/Subsurface/Transmission`), uses energy-preserving multi-scatter GGX, renames `Specular` to `Specular IOR Level`, renames `Clearcoat` to `Coat Weight`, and places `Sheen` at the top microfiber layer.

workflow_steps: Classify each material as Dielectric (`Metallic = 0.0`), Conductor (`Metallic = 1.0`), Refractive Dielectric (`Transmission Weight = 1.0`, `Roughness <= 0.15`, `IOR = 1.45-1.52`), or Coated Dielectric (`Coat Weight = 1.0`, `Coat Roughness = 0.03-0.10`).
Clamp `Base Color` values inside `[0.04, 0.90]` linear for dielectrics and `[0.55, 0.98]` linear for bare polished metals.

When authoring across Blender versions, map Blender 3.6 LTS `Specular` (`0.5`) to Blender 4.0+ `Specular IOR Level` (`0.5`), `Clearcoat` to `Coat Weight`, and `Subsurface` to `Subsurface Weight` (`0..1`) + `Subsurface Scale` (in meters).
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Shader Editor -> Shader -> Principled BSDF (v2 in Blender 4.0+/4.2 LTS/5.1+, v1 in Blender 3.6 LTS).

observable_checks.pass_condition: Linear luminance stays between `0.04` (charcoal) and `0.90` (fresh snow/white paint).
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Pure `0.0` black eats all indirect light or pure `1.0` white causes radioactive GI blowouts.

observable_checks.check: Inspect `Metallic` scalar or texture values on uniform materials.
observable_checks.pass_condition: `Metallic` is `0.0` for plastics/wood/stone/fabric/glass and `1.0` for bare metals.

creative_affordances: Layering a low-roughness `Coat` (`Coat Weight = 1.0`, `Coat Roughness = 0.04`) over a higher-roughness metallic base (`Roughness = 0.35`) creates authentic automotive flake paint and anodized footwear finishes.
Blender 4.0+ microfiber `Sheen` (`Sheen Weight = 0.5-1.0`, `Sheen Roughness = 0.4`) produces velvety grazing rim highlights on suede, nylon, and canvas.

records.title: ORM Channel Packing (Occlusion/Roughness/Metallic) & Linear Non-Color Space Discipline
records.summary: Rules for packing Ambient Occlusion (R), Roughness (G), and Metallic (B) into a single linear RGB texture for glTF 2.0 and enforcing `Non-Color` color space on all non-albedo data textures.
intent_signals: how do I pack AO, Roughness, and Metallic into one ORM texture in Blender
which textures should be set to sRGB vs Non-Color in Blender
normal map or roughness map looks shiny, wrong, or has seam lines
wire glTF Settings node for Ambient Occlusion export in Blender

when_to_apply: Wiring image textures into Principled BSDF for rendering or glTF 2.0 / GLB export.
Auditing material setups in `material-quality-checker` and `mobile-glb-budget`.
when_not_to_apply: Untextured scalar-only materials.

prerequisites: AO, Roughness, and Metallic maps share the same UV layout and resolution.
principles: Color textures (`Base Color`, `Emission`, `Sheen Tint`) store perceptual gamma-encoded values and MUST use `Color Space = sRGB`; all scalar/vector data maps (`Normal`, `Roughness`, `Metallic`, `Ambient Occlusion`, `ORM`, `Alpha`, `Displacement`) store linear math values and MUST use `Color Space = Non-Color`.

Leaving a Roughness map on `sRGB` applies an inverse ~2.2 gamma curve (`0.5^2.2 = 0.218`), making mid-roughness satin materials appear overly wet and glossy; leaving a Normal map on `sRGB` warps the neutral `0.5` flat vector to `0.218` and creates dark seam borders.

Khronos glTF 2.0 packs `metallicRoughnessTexture` with **Green = Roughness (`G`)** and **Blue = Metalness (`B`)**, and supports packing **Red = Ambient Occlusion (`R`)** in the exact same image texture (`ORM`), cutting 3 GPU texture lookups and 3 VRAM allocations down to 1.

Because Principled BSDF has no dedicated Ambient Occlusion socket, Blender's glTF exporter reads baked AO from a shader node group named `glTF Material Output` (or legacy `glTF Settings` with an `Occlusion` input socket) — NEVER multiply baked AO directly into `Base Color` for glTF export.

workflow_steps: Verify every `Image Texture` node in the Shader Editor: set `Base Color` and `Emission` to `sRGB`, and set `ORM`, `Roughness`, `Metallic`, `Normal`, and `Height` to `Non-Color`.

Connect the packed `ORM` `Image Texture` (`Non-Color`) into a `Separate Color` node (`Mode: RGB`): route `Green` -> `Principled BSDF: Roughness`, `Blue` -> `Principled BSDF: Metallic`, and `Red` -> `glTF Material Output: Occlusion`.
Connect the `Normal` `Image Texture` (`Non-Color`) through a `Vector -> Normal Map` node (`Tangent Space`, `Strength = 1.0`) into `Principled BSDF: Normal`.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Shader Editor -> Image Texture (Color Space: Non-Color vs. sRGB) -> Converter -> Separate Color (4.0+) / Separate RGB.

observable_checks.check: Inspect the `Color Space` dropdown on every `Image Texture` node connected to Normal, Roughness, Metallic, or Occlusion.
observable_checks.pass_condition: 100% of data textures are set to `Non-Color`.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Any data map set to `sRGB` distorts surface roughness or bends normals at UV seams.

observable_checks.check: Verify channel routing from `Separate Color` on packed ORM maps.
observable_checks.pass_condition: `R` -> Occlusion, `G` -> Roughness, `B` -> Metallic.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Swapping G and B turns non-metallic rough surfaces into mirror-smooth metals.

observable_checks.check: Check how Ambient Occlusion is wired in materials destined for glTF export.
observable_checks.pass_condition: AO is wired to the `glTF Material Output` (`Occlusion`) socket so it attenuates only indirect ambient light.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Multiplying AO into `Base Color` creates permanent black dirt streaks even under direct flashlight illumination.

creative_affordances: Packing AO + Roughness + Metallic into one ORM texture saves 66% of data-map VRAM and speeds up web loading.
Allows clean separation between direct studio lights and ambient environment occlusion in Three.js.
known_limits: When Blender exports separate Roughness and Metallic grayscale images to GLB, the glTF exporter automatically packs them into one `G+B` texture at export time, but pre-packing `R+G+B` ORM in your texture pipeline avoids redundant source files.

claims.statement: The glTF 2.0 specification requires `metallicRoughnessTexture` to encode metalness in the B (blue) channel and roughness in the G (green) channel using linear transfer functions, while `occlusionTexture` reads from the R (red) channel.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Allowing a single RGB texture to serve as both `occlusionTexture` and `metallicRoughnessTexture`.

records.title: Blender Shader Graph to Khronos glTF 2.0 Export Portability & Extension Matrix
records.summary: Definitive compatibility boundary between Blender-only procedural shader nodes (Noise, Voronoi, ColorRamp, Mix Shader, Shader to RGB, Ambient Occlusion) and the strict Principled BSDF node patterns supported by the glTF 2.0 exporter and KHR material extensions.
intent_signals: why did my Blender materials disappear or turn white when exported to GLB
which Blender shader nodes export to glTF 2.0 and Three.js
do Noise Texture, ColorRamp, or Mix Shader export to GLB
export glass transmission, clearcoat, or sheen from Blender to Three.js
metallic material looks black in threejs r3f shader export

when_to_apply: Planning or auditing materials for any asset that will be exported to `.glb` / `.gltf` (`lighting-material-plan`, `material-quality-checker`, `glb-web-handoff`).
when_not_to_apply: Assets rendered exclusively inside Blender Cycles/EEVEE with zero 3D file interchange.

prerequisites: Target web viewer (`Three.js` / `React Three Fiber`) extension support is known.
principles: Blender's glTF 2.0 exporter does NOT transpile arbitrary Blender shader graphs into GLSL; it pattern-matches specific direct connections into `Principled BSDF` (`Base Color`, `Metallic`, `Roughness`, `Normal`, `Emission`, `Alpha`) and `glTF Material Output` (`Occlusion`).

Any procedural generator (`Noise Texture`, `Voronoi`, `Musgrave`/`Wave`, `Ambient Occlusion`, `Bevel`, `Pointiness`) or remapper (`ColorRamp`, `Map Range`, `Mix Shader`, `Shader to RGB`) connected upstream of Principled BSDF will be silently dropped on GLB export unless baked to image textures first.
UV tiling and offset export ONLY when wired strictly as `Texture Coordinate (UV) -> Mapping (Point/Texture) -> Image Texture`, which translates to `KHR_texture_transform`.

Advanced physical layers on Principled BSDF v2 export as optional Khronos extensions (`Coat` -> `KHR_materials_clearcoat`, `Transmission` -> `KHR_materials_transmission` + `KHR_materials_volume`, `Sheen` -> `KHR_materials_sheen`, `IOR` -> `KHR_materials_ior`, `Specular` -> `KHR_materials_specular`, `Emission Strength > 1` -> `KHR_materials_emissive_strength`), which require `MeshPhysicalMaterial` in Three.js.

workflow_steps: Audit every material's node tree: if any procedural noise, curvature, or `ColorRamp` node is present, bake its output into `Base Color` (sRGB), `ORM` (Non-Color), and `Normal` (Non-Color) image textures before export.
Ensure every exported material has a single `Principled BSDF` wired directly to `Material Output (Surface)` (never through a `Mix Shader` or `Add Shader`).
For refractive glass on mobile web where `KHR_materials_transmission` framebuffer copies are expensive, offer an `Alpha Blend` (`Alpha = 0.25`, `Roughness = 0.08`) fallback profile.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Shader Editor -> Principled BSDF + Image Texture + Mapping + Normal Map + Separate Color + glTF Material Output.

observable_checks.check: Scan the Shader Editor of every GLB-targeted material for procedural texture or converter nodes.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Only `Image Texture`, `UV Map`/`Texture Coordinate`, `Mapping`, `Separate Color`, `Multiply` (for scalar/color factor tinting), `Normal Map`, `Principled BSDF`, and `glTF Material Output` are present.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: `Noise Texture`, `ColorRamp`, `Shader to RGB`, or `Mix Shader` is wired directly into the exported shader.

observable_checks.check: Verify blend/alpha settings on transparent or cutout materials.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Foliage/decals use `Alpha Clip` (`MASK`) with explicit cutoff; glass uses `Alpha Blend` (`BLEND`) or `KHR_materials_transmission`; opaque surfaces use `Opaque` (`OPAQUE`).
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Opaque meshes accidentally left on `Alpha Blend` cause Z-sorting transparency flicker in Three.js.

observable_checks.check: Verify that any used `KHR_materials_*` extensions are listed in the web handoff report.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Transmission, Clearcoat, Sheen, IOR, and Emissive Strength extensions are documented for the Three.js team.

creative_affordances: Authoring rich procedural wear/grime in Blender and baking to a clean 2K `Base Color + ORM + Normal` triplet preserves 100% of the procedural art direction while running at 60 FPS on any WebGL device.
`KHR_materials_emissive_strength` allows neon cyberpunk accents to drive Three.js post-processing UnrealBloomPass selectively when `emissiveIntensity > 1.0`.

records.title: Three-Point Studio Lighting Ratios, Area Light Angular Size & HDRI Balance
records.summary: Physically based studio lighting methodology governing Key-to-Fill illuminance ratios (EV contrast), Area light physical size vs. shadow penumbra softness, grazing Rim/kicker placement, and neutral HDRI environment fill.
intent_signals: set up studio three-point lighting for a product hero or character portrait
lighting looks flat, washed out, or has harsh black shadows
balance HDRI environment lighting with key and rim area lights
how to light dark glossy or metallic products in Blender

when_to_apply: Planning or auditing lighting for product hero scenes, product grids, or character portraits (`lighting-material-plan`, `lighting-quality-checker`, `product-hero-scene-planner`, `character-portrait`).
when_not_to_apply: Pure sun/sky exterior architectural daylight studies where a single physical sun + sky atmosphere dominates.

prerequisites: Subject is modeled at 1:1 metric scale (`1 BU = 1m`) so Area light power (Watts) and inverse-square falloff (`1/d^2`) behave physically.
principles: Form perception depends on luminance contrast between lit and shadowed planes; an equal `1:1` Key-to-Fill ratio erases volume, whereas a `2:1` to `4:1` ratio (commercial/editorial) or `8:1` ratio (dramatic/cyberpunk) sculpts clear 3D dimensionality.
Shadow penumbra softness and specular highlight ribbon width are controlled by the **angular size** of the Area light relative to the subject (`Light Size / Distance`), NOT by light wattage.

Highly reflective metals and dark glossy plastics do not show diffuse light; they reflect the bright cards/softboxes around them, requiring large soft Area lights (or gradient light cards) positioned along reflection vectors plus a dark negative-fill environment.
An HDRI World environment should serve as a subordinate ambient/reflection base (`0.2` to `0.5` Strength, `-1.5` to `-2.5 EV` below the Key light) rather than overpowering directional studio lights.

workflow_steps: Start from a pitch-black world (`Strength = 0`) and place the **Key Area Light** at `30-45 deg` azimuth and `30-45 deg` elevation from the camera-subject axis, sized `1.5x-3.0x` the subject's diameter for soft wrap.

Add the **Fill Light** on the opposite side (`-45 to -60 deg` azimuth) at `2x` the Key's size and `0.125x-0.5x` the Key's illuminance (`4:1` to `2:1` ratio) to lift shadows without creating a competing secondary sharp shadow.

Place the **Rim / Kicker Area Strip Light** behind the subject (`135-165 deg` azimuth) to separate the silhouette from the background, then bring up a low-saturation studio HDRI at `Strength = 0.25-0.45` solely to fill metallic specular reflections.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Object Data Properties (Light) -> Area Light (Shape: Rectangle/Disk, Power in Watts, Size X/Y, Spread); Shader Editor (World) -> Environment Texture -> Background.

observable_checks.check: Inspect the False Color view transform or luminance difference between the key-lit side and fill-lit side of the subject.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Key side is at least 1 to 3 stops (2:1 to 8:1) brighter than the fill side, with one clear primary shadow direction.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Equal left/right light intensity flattens the subject and casts crossed double shadows.

observable_checks.check: Inspect the subject's shadow-side contour against the background in grayscale.
observable_checks.pass_condition: A crisp rim highlight or background value gradient separates 100% of the subject silhouette from the backdrop.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Dark subject shadow side merges indistinguishably into a dark background.

observable_checks.check: Mute the Key, Fill, and Rim lights and inspect the HDRI-only contribution.
observable_checks.pass_condition: HDRI alone provides soft ambient reflection fill without blowing out diffuse exposure.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: High-contrast outdoor sun HDRI at Strength >= 1.0 washes out the studio rig and tints white materials orange/blue.

creative_affordances: Using a narrow `Spread` angle (`30-60 deg`) on Cycles Area lights acts like a physical honeycomb grid/egg-crate, keeping key light focused on the product while plunging the background floor into moody shadow.
Split-complementary color temperature contrast (e.g., `5200K` neutral-warm Key + `7500K` cool-cyan Fill or Magenta/Cyan cyberpunk rims) creates instant cinematic separation.
known_limits: Area light `Spread` beam narrowing is accurately raytraced in Cycles and supported in EEVEE Next (Blender 4.2 LTS), but is ignored in Legacy EEVEE (Blender 3.6 LTS).
Blender Area lights do not export to standard glTF 2.0 unless `KHR_lights_punctual` is enabled (which only supports Point, Spot, and Directional lights — not rectangular Area softboxes).

claims.statement: In physically based rendering, shadow edge softness (penumbra width) is determined by the subtended solid angle of the emitter (`Size / Distance`), whereas emitter `Power` (Watts) only scales radiometric intensity.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Fundamental radiometric law.

records.title: Physical Camera Sensor Size, Focal Length Compression, Tilt-Shift & Depth of Field
records.summary: Optical rules for selecting full-frame (36mm) equivalent focal lengths by scene domain, preventing wide-angle perspective distortion on products/portraits, maintaining parallel architectural verticals via Lens Shift Y, and calibrating physical f-stop depth of field.
intent_signals: what camera focal length and f-stop should I use for a product or portrait render
product or character face looks warped and fish-eyed in close-up
keep vertical walls straight in an architectural interior render
depth of field is either completely blurry or not blurring at all

when_to_apply: Configuring camera optics, framing, and depth of field in `camera-composition`, `composition-quality-checker`, `product-hero-scene-planner`, `character-portrait`, `interior-scene`, and `environment-shot`.
when_not_to_apply: Asset-only geometry preparation where no camera or render view is configured.

prerequisites: Scene modeled at true metric scale (`1 BU = 1m`) and Camera Sensor Width locked to `36 mm` (Full Frame standard).
principles: Perspective distortion is governed by camera-to-subject distance; using a wide lens (`< 35mm` on a 36mm sensor) close to a product or face exaggerates near features (nose/toe-box) by 30-50%, whereas `50mm-105mm` lenses allow a flattering working distance with natural proportion compression.

Physical Depth of Field circle-of-confusion radius scales inversely with f-stop (`D = f / N`) and quadratically with focus distance; if a 0.30m sneaker is modeled at 30 meters by mistake, `f/2.8` produces almost zero blur unless the scene scale is corrected to meters.

In architectural interiors and exteriors, tilting the camera up or down (`Rotation X != 90 deg`) introduces 3-point perspective where vertical walls converge; locking `Rotation X = 90.0 deg` and framing vertically via `Camera -> Lens -> Shift Y` preserves strict 2-point parallel verticals.
For e-commerce product grids and UI cards, leaving 25-35% intentional negative space (or a dedicated copy-safe third) prevents text overlays and badges from colliding with the hero silhouette.

workflow_steps: Set Camera `Sensor Fit = Auto`, `Sensor Width = 36 mm`, and choose focal length by domain: **Product Hero** `65mm-105mm` (`85mm` default), **Character Portrait** `85mm-135mm`, **Interior Archviz** `24mm-35mm` (with `Rotation X = 90 deg` + `Shift Y`), **Environment Wide Shot** `24mm-35mm`.
Place an `Empty` object (`Focus_Target`) at the nearest hero focal feature (e.g., front eye or product logo badge) and assign it as the Camera's `Depth of Field -> Focus Object`.

Set `F-Stop` according to subject size at 1:1 meter scale: `f/4.0 - f/8.0` for tabletop products (`0.15m - 0.5m` size) so the front and mid-body stay sharp while the background softens; `f/2.0 - f/4.0` for human portraits.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Object Data Properties (Camera) -> Lens (Focal Length, Shift X/Y), Depth of Field (Focus Object, F-Stop, Blades), Sensor (Width: 36mm).

observable_checks.check: Inspect Camera Focal Length (at 36mm sensor width) for product hero and character portrait shots.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Focal length is `>= 50 mm` (`65-105 mm` preferred for products, `85-135 mm` for portraits).
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Default `50mm` or `<35mm` lens used at macro distance, warping product geometry.

observable_checks.check: Check Camera `Rotation X` on interior and architectural eye-level shots.
observable_checks.pass_condition: `Rotation X = 90.0 deg` (level horizon) with vertical composition adjusted via `Lens Shift Y`.

records.title: AgX vs. Filmic Color Management, EEVEE Next (4.2+) vs. Cycles & Output Bit Depth
records.summary: Version-aware rendering and color management architecture comparing `AgX` (Blender 4.0+ default) vs. `Filmic` (3.6 LTS default) vs. `Khronos PBR Neutral`, `Cycles` path tracing vs. `EEVEE Next` (4.2 LTS) / `Legacy EEVEE` (3.6 LTS), and 8-bit/16-bit PNG vs. linear OpenEXR output.
intent_signals: should I use AgX, Filmic, or Khronos PBR Neutral in Blender
what changed in EEVEE Next in Blender 4.2 LTS vs Cycles
fix neon colors clipping to yellow or cyan in Blender renders
prevent color banding in dark studio background gradients

when_to_apply: Selecting color management (`color-management-decision`), render engine (`cycles-vs-eevee-decision`), and output file format (`output-format-decision`).
Synchronizing Blender lookdev with Three.js / React Three Fiber web viewers.
when_not_to_apply: Geometry-only container checks with no rendering or color pipeline.

prerequisites: Target Blender version (3.6 LTS vs. 4.2 LTS / 5.1+) and final delivery medium (direct web sRGB vs. Nuke/Resolve/Compositor grading) are known.
principles: Per-channel display transforms (`Standard` and `Filmic`) clip individual R, G, or B channels sequentially at high exposure, skewing intense red/blue/magenta lights into harsh yellow/cyan/white (`Notorious Six`); **AgX** (Blender 4.0+ default) attenuates chroma smoothly toward white before channel clipping, preserving natural highlight roll-off.

**Khronos PBR Neutral** (added in Blender 4.2 LTS) is specifically engineered for e-commerce product photography where exact sRGB brand swatch fidelity in midtones is required without filmic hue shifts.

Blender 4.2 LTS replaced Legacy EEVEE with **EEVEE Next**, introducing screen-space raytraced indirect lighting, virtual shadow maps, and horizon scan, while removing the legacy EEVEE `Bloom` checkbox in favor of the Viewport/Render Compositor `Glare` (`Fog Glow` / `Bloom`) node.

Saving smooth dark studio vignettes to 8-bit PNG (256 levels per channel) causes visible staircase color banding; use **16-bit PNG** (with `Dither = 1.0-2.0`) for direct delivery or **16-bit half-float OpenEXR (DWAA/ZIP)** for linear scene-referred compositing (note: OpenEXR stores raw linear data and does NOT bake the AgX/Filmic view transform).

workflow_steps: Set `Display Device = sRGB` and select `View Transform`: `AgX` (`Look: Medium High Contrast` or `Punchy`) for general/cinematic/neon scenes in Blender 4.0+; `Khronos PBR Neutral` for color-critical e-commerce in 4.2+; `Filmic` (`Medium High Contrast`) if constrained to Blender 3.6 LTS.

Choose Render Engine: `Cycles` (`GPU Compute`, `Noise Threshold = 0.01`, `Max Samples = 256-1024`, `OpenImageDenoise` with `Albedo and Normal` passes) for refractive glass, caustics, or baking; `EEVEE Next` (4.2+) for fast turntables and stylization.

In Blender 4.2+ EEVEE Next or Cycles, add a `Filter -> Glare` (`Bloom` or `Fog Glow`, `Mix = -0.85`) node in the Compositor with Viewport Compositor set to `Always` instead of looking for the removed EEVEE Bloom property.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Render Properties -> Color Management (View Transform, Look, Exposure) & Film -> Transparent; Output Properties -> Output (File Format: PNG 16-bit or OpenEXR) & Post Processing -> Dither.

records.title: Armature Joint Hierarchy, Transform Alignment & 4-Bone Linear Blend Skinning
records.summary: Skeletal rigging invariants for Blender and glTF 2.0: shared mesh/armature world origin with applied unit transforms, separation of deform bones from IK control rigs, consistent bone roll, and normalized <=4-bone vertex weight limits.
intent_signals: character mesh explodes or stretches when exported to GLB
how many bone influences per vertex are allowed in glTF and Three.js
limit and normalize vertex weights in Blender Weight Paint
separate Rigify control bones from deform bones for export

when_to_apply: Rigging and skinning any character, creature, or articulated mechanical asset destined for animation playback or glTF/GLB export (`glb-animation-handoff`).
when_not_to_apply: Static unrigged props.

prerequisites: Mesh topology has sufficient joint bending loops (`knowledge.quad-dominant-subdivision-topology`) and rest pose is symmetric.
principles: Both the Skinned Mesh and the Armature object MUST share the exact same world origin `(0, 0, 0)` with applied Location `(0,0,0)`, Rotation `(0,0,0)`, and Scale `(1,1,1)` BEFORE binding (`Armature Deform`); mismatched object transforms cause double-transform or 100x scale explosions in glTF viewers.

Standard glTF 2.0 and WebGL GPU skinning (`JOINTS_0` and `WEIGHTS_0` `VEC4` vertex attributes) evaluate Linear Blend Skinning (LBS) with at most **4 bone influences per vertex** whose weights MUST sum strictly to `1.0`.

Blender's `Preserve Volume` checkbox on the Armature modifier uses Dual Quaternion Skinning (DQS), which is NOT supported by glTF 2.0 or Three.js; always preview and weight-paint with `Preserve Volume = False` when targeting web/game engines.
Non-uniform scaling on a parent deform bone shears child bone rotation matrices in Linear Blend Skinning; keep all deform bone scales uniform `(1,1,1)` or disable `Inherit Scale` on child bones.

workflow_steps: In Object Mode at Rest Pose, select both the Mesh and the Armature and run `Ctrl+A -> All Transforms` so both sit at `(0,0,0)` with scale `(1,1,1)`.

In Weight Paint Mode, select all deform vertex groups (`Subset: Deform Pose Bones`), run `Weights -> Limit Total` (`Limit = 4`), and immediately run `Weights -> Normalize All` (`Lock Active = False`).
Uncheck `Bone Properties -> Deform` on all IK pole targets, widget shapes, and root-motion helper bones, and enable `Animation -> Armature -> Export Deformation Bones Only` in the glTF 2.0 exporter.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Weight Paint Mode -> Weights -> Limit Total (4) & Normalize All; Armature Modifier (Preserve Volume: False); Bone Properties -> Deform.

observable_checks.fail_indicator: Mesh has scale `(0.01, 0.01, 0.01)` while Armature has `(1, 1, 1)`, causing inverseBindMatrices mismatch on export.

observable_checks.pass_condition: Every vertex has `<= 4` deform bone weights summing to `1.000`.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Vertices weighted to 6-8 bones get truncated on GLB export, leaving unnormalized weights that pull vertices toward world origin `(0,0,0)`.

observable_checks.check: Verify Armature modifier settings during pose testing.
observable_checks.pass_condition: `Preserve Volume` is unchecked when validating deformations for glTF/Three.js.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Elbows/wrists look thick in Blender with `Preserve Volume` on, then candy-wrapper collapse after GLB export.

creative_affordances: Adding a dedicated twist deform bone along the forearm and thigh distributes 180-degree pronation rotation smoothly under standard 4-bone Linear Blend Skinning without needing Dual Quaternions.
Rigid mechanical props (hinged laptop lid, watch hands, turret) can be parented directly to individual bones (`Parent to Bone`) with zero vertex skinning overhead.
known_limits: Blender 4.0+ replaced numbered 32-slot Armature layers (`armature.layers`) with named `Bone Collections` (`armature.collections`); older rigging scripts referencing `layers[n]` fail on Blender 4.0+/4.2 LTS.

claims.statement: Standard glTF 2.0 skinning stores joint indices and weights in `JOINTS_0` and `WEIGHTS_0` `VEC4` accessors (4 components per vertex) and requires the sum of weights for each vertex to equal `1.0`.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: While a second `JOINTS_1`/`WEIGHTS_1` set is theoretically permitted by spec, standard WebGL shaders in Three.js bind 4 influences (`JOINTS_0`/`WEIGHTS_0`).
