records.title: NLA Action Baking, Constraint Sampling, and Shape Key (Morph Target) Export Rules
records.summary: Rules for baking IK/constraint rigs into visual FK keyframe clips on NLA tracks and managing Shape Key (Morph Target) memory overhead for glTF 2.0 export.
intent_signals: bake IK constraints to FK keyframes for glb export
organize multiple animation clips on NLA tracks for Three.js AnimationMixer
export shape keys morph targets without exploding glb file size

when_to_apply: When exporting character animations (Idle, Walk, Run) or mechanical rigged assemblies to .glb.
When choosing between skeletal armature animation and Shape Keys (Morph Targets) for facial expressions or soft deformations.
when_not_to_apply: When animations remain exclusively inside a native .blend file for offline Cycles rendering.
When animations are procedural camera orbits driven by React Three Fiber at runtime.

prerequisites: Scene frame rate (24, 30, or 60 fps) is locked before baking and each clip is stored as a named Action on an NLA Track.
principles: Core glTF 2.0 animation channels only evaluate node translation, rotation, scale (TRS), or morph target weights; Blender IK solvers, drivers, and constraints must be baked into visual TRS keyframes.
Pushing named Actions down onto separate NLA Tracks ensures the glTF exporter emits distinct named AnimationClips for THREE.AnimationMixer.
Shape Keys (glTF Morph Targets) store per-vertex position/normal deltas; attaching dozens of shape keys to a 100k-vertex unified body mesh multiplies buffer size across every vertex.

workflow_steps: Bake complex IK chains and constraints to deform bones using Pose -> Animation -> Bake Action with Visual Keying and Clear Constraints enabled.
Push each baked clip (Idle, Walk, OpenLid) onto its own named NLA track in the NLA Editor and verify Optimize Animation Size is enabled on export.
Isolate meshes that require Shape Keys (e.g., separate head/face mesh from body) so morph delta buffers only cover deforming vertices.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Pose Mode -> Pose -> Animation -> Bake Action; NLA Editor -> Push Down Action; File -> Export -> glTF 2.0 -> Animation.

observable_checks.fail_indicator: Exported .glb contains a single Action.001 or merges unrelated tracks together.

observable_checks.pass_condition: Shape Keys reside only on the sub-mesh that deforms and total morph buffer stays within budget.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Dozens of Shape Keys are attached to a full-body high-poly mesh, bloating .glb size by tens of megabytes.

creative_affordances: Enables interactive product states (lid opening, exploded assembly view, character idle loops) triggered via @react-three/drei useAnimations.
Allows expressive facial micro-expressions via Morph Targets combined with skeletal head and neck rotation.
known_limits: glTF 2.0 does not export arbitrary Blender modifier parameter animations without baking to meshes or morph targets.
Blender 4.4+ introduced slotted Actions (Action Slots), allowing one Action datablock to store tracks for multiple objects.

claims.statement: Core glTF 2.0 animation channels target node translation, rotation, scale, or morph target weights; Blender constraints and IK solvers must be sampled into TRS keyframes during export.
claims.scope: Khronos glTF 2.0 specification and Blender glTF 2.0 exporter.

records.title: Rigid Body, Cloth, and Physics Simulation Cache Baking vs. Real-Time Tradeoffs
records.summary: Principles for setting solver substeps, collision margins, and baking Blender physics simulations (Rigid Body, Cloth, Soft Body, Fluid) for offline rendering or keyframe interchange.
intent_signals: bake rigid body physics simulation to object keyframes
fix cloth simulation self-intersection tunneling and collision margin
prepare settled physics prop piles or draped fabric in Blender

when_to_apply: When simulating cloth drapes, falling rigid-body piles, cables, or dynamic settled poses in Blender.
When preparing physics-settled props or baked rigid-body transform animations for export.
when_not_to_apply: When exporting raw Mantaflow fluid voxel grids or per-frame cloth vertex caches directly to a lightweight mobile .glb.
When simple manual placement or Geometry Nodes scatter achieves the layout without simulation instability.

prerequisites: Real-world metric scale (1 BU = 1m), applied scale (1,1,1), and Origin to Center of Mass on active Rigid Body objects.
principles: Blender physics solvers assume 1 Blender Unit equals 1 meter for gravity (-9.81 m/s^2); unapplied or 100x centimeter scale makes simulations appear slow and floaty.
Convex Hull and primitive collision shapes (Box, Sphere, Capsule) evaluate orders of magnitude faster and more stably than triangle Mesh colliders.
Baking Rigid Body motion to TRS keyframes (Bake to Keyframes) produces standard node animations that export cleanly to glTF 2.0.

workflow_steps: Apply scale (Ctrl+A -> Scale) and set Origin to Center of Mass (Volume) on all active Rigid Body objects before simulating.
Use Convex Hull collision shapes with 0.002m-0.005m collision margin and 10+ substeps per frame to prevent fast-object tunneling.
Freeze static settled poses via Convert to Mesh, or bake dynamic rigid bodies via Object -> Rigid Body -> Bake to Keyframes.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Physics Properties -> Rigid Body / Cloth; Scene Properties -> Rigid Body World -> Cache -> Bake All Dynamics; Object -> Rigid Body -> Bake to Keyframes.

observable_checks.pass_condition: Objects fall and tumble at physically plausible speeds without pivoting around a distant world origin.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Objects pivot wildly around (0,0,0) or float in slow motion due to unapplied scale.

observable_checks.check: Verify physics caches are explicitly baked (Bake All Dynamics or Bake to Keyframes) before rendering or exporting.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Scrubbing timeline or rendering out-of-order frames produces deterministic positions.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Unbaked simulation snaps or resets mid-render.

creative_affordances: Cloth pressure (Physics -> Cloth -> Pressure) rapidly sculpts believable cushions, pillows, inflated jackets, and padded footwear panels.
Rigid Body drop simulations create organic clutter piles (cables, rocks, coins) free of manual intersection.
known_limits: Variable-topology simulations (Mantaflow liquid meshes, remeshed fracture) cannot be exported as glTF morph targets and require Alembic (.abc) or USD (.usdc) for offline DCC pipelines.

claims.statement: Blender's Rigid Body -> Bake to Keyframes converts simulated rigid-body motion into standard object Location and Rotation keyframes and removes the active simulation solver dependency.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Standard Blender Physics workflow documented in Blender Manual.

records.title: Volumetric Lighting, Principled Volume, and Real-Time Depth Fog Tradeoffs
records.summary: Decision rules for using Principled Volume shaders in Cycles/EEVEE versus Mist Pass compositing or lightweight scene fog for web and real-time targets.
intent_signals: add volumetric fog haze and god rays in Blender Cycles or EEVEE
fix black render when using Principled Volume on World shader with Sun light
translate Blender atmospheric depth fog to Three.js React Three Fiber

when_to_apply: When adding atmospheric haze, crepuscular god rays, or depth separation to environment and hero product renders.
When deciding how to translate Blender atmospheric mood to Three.js / React Three Fiber.
when_not_to_apply: When attaching Principled Volume to the unbounded World output in Cycles with a Sun light (infinite volume blocks distant Sun lamps).

prerequisites: Volume bounds are contained within a finite domain cube mesh rather than an unbounded World shader in Cycles.
principles: In Cycles, attaching a Volume shader to the World output fills infinite space and completely attenuates light from Sun lamps and HDRIs evaluated at infinity.
A bounded domain cube with Principled Volume (Density 0.005-0.03, Anisotropy 0.3-0.7) produces directional light shafts without blocking distant environment lights.
Open-air volumetric fog does not export inside .glb files; web viewers reproduce atmospheric depth using THREE.Fog or THREE.FogExp2.

workflow_steps: Create a bounded fog cube around the staging area with Surface disconnected and Principled Volume connected to the Volume material output.
Set Density to 0.005-0.03 and Anisotropy to 0.4-0.6 for forward-scattered backlight beams, or use the Mist render pass for zero-noise composited depth haze.
Exclude the volume domain cube from .glb exports and document equivalent <fog> parameters in the web handoff spec.

records.title: Foreground / Midground / Background Depth Layering and Cyclorama Staging
records.summary: Compositional staging patterns for studio cycloramas (infinity curves) and 3-plane environment depth layering (foreground framing, lit midground focal hero, low-contrast atmospheric background).
intent_signals: stage a hero product on a seamless studio cyclorama infinity backdrop
compose foreground midground background depth layers in an environment shot
separate hero silhouette from background clutter using luminance contrast

when_to_apply: When staging a hero product on a seamless studio backdrop or pedestal.
When composing an interior room, diorama, or stylized exterior environment with strong visual depth.

prerequisites: Primary camera angle, aspect ratio (16:9, 1:1, 4:5), and hero subject Z = 0 ground contact are normalized.
principles: Three-plane depth staging separates Foreground (framing/reflections), Midground (highest-contrast focal hero), and Background (lower-contrast cyclorama or fog-softened architecture).
An L-shaped backdrop with a large multi-segment Bevel modifier (radius 1.5m-3.0m, 16-32 segments) creates a seamless cyclorama infinity curve with no harsh horizon crease.
Isolating studio backdrops and environment dressing in a dedicated Staging collection ensures standalone hero .glb exports never leak backdrop meshes.

workflow_steps: Construct an L-shaped studio backdrop or 3-plane environment layout in a dedicated Staging_Env collection separate from the hero subject.
Apply a 16-32 segment Bevel modifier (Width 2.0m) with Shade Smooth to the floor-to-wall corner for a seamless studio infinity curve.
Verify grayscale luminance separation (>= 3:1 edge contrast) between the midground hero silhouette and the background value.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Modifiers -> Generate -> Bevel (Cyclorama Curve); Object Properties -> Visibility -> Shadow Catcher (Cycles); Outliner -> Collection Visibility.

observable_checks.check: Inspect the camera view luminance contrast between the hero subject and background.
observable_checks.pass_condition: The midground hero subject reads clearly as a distinct silhouette against the background value.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Hero edges blend into mid-tone background clutter with identical luminance.

observable_checks.check: Verify that cyclorama, pedestal, and background props reside in a separate collection from the hero asset.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Hero asset can be isolated or exported independently without geometry surgery.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Backdrop and hero meshes are joined into one object.

creative_affordances: Sweeping a spot light with a wide Blend (0.8-1.0) onto a dark cyclorama creates a natural radial vignette behind the hero subject.
Using Cycles Shadow Catcher on a ground plane allows transparent-background PNG renders that retain grounded contact shadows.
known_limits: Shadow Catcher is a Cycles-native feature; for EEVEE or Three.js web viewers, use baked ambient occlusion planes or @react-three/drei <ContactShadows>.

claims.statement: In Cycles, enabling Shadow Catcher on a ground mesh together with Render Properties -> Film -> Transparent renders only the subject and its ground shadows into the alpha channel for compositing.

records.title: Triangle, Draw Call, Texture VRAM, and File Size Budgets by Target Tier
records.summary: Quantitative performance budget envelopes across Mobile Web, Desktop Web / E-Commerce Hero, Real-Time Engine, and Offline Rendering tiers.
intent_signals: check mobile web and desktop triangle count and draw call budgets
calculate uncompressed 4K RGBA8 texture GPU VRAM memory usage
set performance budget acceptance criteria for a web GLB asset

when_to_apply: When setting acceptance criteria and optimization targets before modeling, baking, or exporting a 3D asset.
When auditing whether a scene or .glb file fits its target deployment platform.
when_not_to_apply: Do not enforce mobile draw-call limits on a single-frame offline Cycles print render unless viewport responsiveness is degraded.

prerequisites: Target deployment tier (mobile_web, desktop_web_hero, desktop_realtime_scene, or offline_render) is specified.
principles: Real-time 3D performance is governed by four orthogonal budgets: evaluated triangle count, draw calls (mesh primitives x material slots), uncompressed GPU texture VRAM, and network .glb payload size.

Standard PNG and JPEG textures stored in a .glb decompress into raw RGBA8 texel buffers (+33% for mipmaps) in GPU VRAM: a single 4096x4096 RGBA8 texture consumes ~89.4 MB of VRAM regardless of its PNG disk size.
Merging static meshes that share a texture atlas and removing duplicate material slots keeps WebGL draw calls within mobile envelopes (<= 15 per hero asset).

workflow_steps: Measure evaluated triangle count (with active export modifiers enabled) and distinct mesh-primitive draw calls (Objects x Material Slots).
Cap mobile web hero assets at <= 35,000 triangles, <= 15 draw calls, <= 2048px textures (KTX2 recommended), and <= 5 MB .glb payload.
Cap desktop web hero assets at <= 100,000 triangles, <= 30 draw calls, <= 2048-4096px textures, and <= 15 MB .glb payload.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Viewport Overlays -> Statistics; Outliner -> Blender File -> Materials / Images; glTF 2.0 Export Manifest.

observable_checks.check: Measure evaluated triangle count in Viewport Statistics with active export modifiers enabled.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Evaluated triangle count is within the target tier envelope (<= 35k mobile hero, <= 100k desktop hero).
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Base cage is 10k tris, but an uncounted Level 3 Subsurf modifier exports 640k tris.

observable_checks.check: Count distinct exported mesh primitives (Objects x Material Slots per Object).
observable_checks.pass_condition: Primitive/material count stays within the draw-call budget (<= 15 mobile hero, <= 30 desktop hero).
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Dozens of duplicate materials (Material.001, Material.002) fragment the asset into 80+ draw calls.

creative_affordances: Allocating 70% of the triangle budget to silhouette bevels and 30% to planar interiors makes a 40k-triangle web asset look like a 500k CAD model.
Packing Ambient Occlusion, Roughness, and Metallic into one ORM map cuts texture sampler count and VRAM by two-thirds.
known_limits: iOS Safari frequently terminates WebGL contexts when total canvas and uncompressed texture VRAM exceeds ~256-384 MB.

claims.statement: Standard PNG and JPEG textures stored in a .glb are decompressed into raw RGBA8 texel buffers (+33% for mipmaps) when uploaded to the GPU in WebGL/Three.js, whereas KTX2 (KHR_texture_basisu) remains block-compressed in GPU VRAM.
claims.scope: Khronos glTF 2.0 KHR_texture_basisu specification and Three.js KTX2Loader.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Confirmed in Khronos KHR_texture_basisu specification and 3D Commerce Asset Creation Guidelines.

source_refs.locator: 3D Commerce Asset Creation Guidelines — Texture Memory & Draw Calls
Khronos 3D Commerce Asset Creation Guidelines — Performance Budgets

records.title: Level of Detail (LOD0–LOD3) Hierarchy, Planar Dissolve, and UV-Safe Decimation
records.summary: Rules for generating LOD0-LOD3 mesh cascades using Decimate (Planar) and UV-seam-preserving Decimate (Collapse) without destroying UV islands or silhouette fidelity.
intent_signals: generate LOD0 LOD1 LOD2 cascade with Blender Decimate modifier
reduce mesh polygon count without destroying UV seams or baked normal maps
use Planar dissolve and Vertex Group masks for safe mesh decimation

when_to_apply: When reducing an over-budget mesh for desktop or mobile web delivery.
When building multi-tier LOD cascades (LOD0, LOD1, LOD2) for distance-switched 3D scenes.
when_not_to_apply: When reducing an animated character face or limb joint that requires strict quad deformation loops (use quad retopology instead of triangulated Decimate Collapse).

prerequisites: Mesh manifold hygiene (Merge by Distance), scale application (1,1,1), and UV seams / sharp edges are marked on LOD0.
principles: Decimate (Planar) with Delimit set to UV and Sharp dissolves redundant coplanar interior polygons losslessly without altering silhouettes or UV island boundaries.
Progressive LOD cascades (LOD1 at 50%, LOD2 at 25%, LOD3 at 10%) must preserve UV seam borders so all LOD tiers share the exact same baked texture set without multiplying VRAM.
Vertex Group masking inside Decimate (Collapse) protects high-attention hero details (logos, eyelets, rims) while concentrating reduction on flat or underside regions.

workflow_steps: Run Decimate -> Planar (Angle Limit 2-5 deg, Delimit: UV, Sharp, Material) first to strip coplanar grid subdivisions.
Generate LOD1 (0.5 ratio) and LOD2 (0.25 ratio) using Decimate -> Collapse with UV seam preservation and a protective Vertex Group mask on hero features.
Verify that all LOD meshes share the single LOD0 material/texture atlas and name nodes deterministically (Asset_LOD0, Asset_LOD1, Asset_LOD2).
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Modifiers -> Generate -> Decimate (Planar / Collapse / Un-Subdivide); Object Data Properties -> Vertex Groups.

observable_checks.check: Assign the LOD0 baked normal/basecolor material to LOD1 and LOD2 and inspect UV seam borders.
observable_checks.pass_condition: All LOD tiers share the same material and display zero UV texture tearing along seams.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: UV seams collapse across island boundaries on LOD1/LOD2, causing visible texture shifts.

observable_checks.check: Overlay LOD0 and LOD1 at expected switching distance in camera view.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Outer silhouette contour matches within 1-2 pixels at the transition distance.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Aggressive decimation flattens curved rims, causing a jarring silhouette pop.

creative_affordances: Vertex-group-masked decimation preserves 100% of the polygons on a sneaker's hero branding badge while reducing the rubber sole tread by 65%.
Pairs directly with @react-three/drei <Detailed> component for automatic camera-distance LOD switching.
known_limits: glTF 2.0 core does not define a universal built-in LOD node; Three.js/R3F apps switch named *_LOD0/*_LOD1 nodes via THREE.LOD or <Detailed>.

claims.statement: Blender's Decimate modifier in Planar mode supports Delimit flags for Normal, Material, Seam, Sharp, and UVs, preventing face dissolution across UV island boundaries.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Confirmed in Blender Manual — Decimate Modifier (Planar mode options).

blender_versions.version_notes: Decimate modifier modes (Collapse, Un-Subdivide, Planar) are stable across Blender 3.x-5.x. Verified against Blender 4.5.15 LTS and 5.2.3 LTS documentation (live runtime: Not Run).

records.title: KTX2 / Basis Universal Texture Compression vs. Draco and Meshopt Geometry Compression
records.summary: Decision matrix for choosing between Draco (KHR_draco_mesh_compression), Meshopt (EXT_meshopt_compression), and KTX2 (KHR_texture_basisu) based on bottleneck type (network payload vs. GPU VRAM vs. CPU decode time).
intent_signals: choose between Draco vs Meshopt vs KTX2 Basis Universal compression
compress glb textures in GPU VRAM with KTX2 UASTC and ETC1S
reduce glb file download size and configure Three.js DRACOLoader KTX2Loader

when_to_apply: When optimizing .glb assets for web delivery, mobile browsers, or React Three Fiber.
When deciding whether an asset's primary bottleneck is geometry buffer size or texture VRAM.
when_not_to_apply: When archiving uncompressed master interchange files for further editing in Blender or Substance.
Do not apply lossy ETC1S compression to tangent-space Normal Maps (use UASTC for normal maps).

prerequisites: Baseline .glb asset is inspected to determine the byte share between mesh buffers and embedded image textures.
principles: Draco and Meshopt compress vertex/index geometry buffers over the network, whereas KTX2 (KHR_texture_basisu) compresses textures both over the network AND inside GPU VRAM (transcoding to BC7/ASTC/ETC2).
KTX2 UASTC preserves high-frequency non-color vectors required for tangent-space Normal and ORM maps, whereas KTX2 ETC1S is suited for diffuse/albedo maps prioritizing small file size.
Draco achieves the smallest network size for dense static meshes, while Meshopt decodes significantly faster in WASM and also compresses morph target and animation keyframe buffers.

workflow_steps: Inspect the .glb byte breakdown between geometry buffers and images before selecting compression tools.
Enable Draco compression (14-bit position, 10-bit normal, 12-bit texcoord) for geometry-heavy static assets or use Meshopt for animated/morph assets.
Encode Normal and ORM textures with KTX2 UASTC and diffuse textures with KTX2 ETC1S, and document required loader decoders (DRACOLoader, MeshoptDecoder, KTX2Loader) in the web handoff.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: File -> Export -> glTF 2.0 -> Compression -> Draco; Post-export CLI optimization (gltf-transform / gltfpack) for KTX2 and Meshopt.

observable_checks.check: Inspect the byte share of buffers vs. images in the .glb export manifest.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Compression strategy matches the dominant bottleneck (KTX2/resize for image-heavy assets; Draco/Meshopt for geometry-heavy assets).
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Draco is enabled on a texture-bound asset while 4K uncompressed PNGs are left untouched.

observable_checks.check: Inspect extensionsRequired in the exported .glb (KHR_draco_mesh_compression, EXT_meshopt_compression, KHR_texture_basisu).
observable_checks.pass_condition: Every required glTF extension is documented in the handoff contract so the frontend configures the matching Three.js decoder.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Compressed .glb fails to load at runtime because the frontend GLTFLoader lacks the required decoder.

creative_affordances: Combining 2K KTX2 textures with Draco/Meshopt geometry compression routinely turns a 45 MB raw .glb into a 3.2 MB instant-loading web hero asset.
gltf-transform CLI pipelines can automate KTX2 + Meshopt optimization after clean baseline .glb export from Blender.
known_limits: Blender's built-in glTF 2.0 exporter includes native Draco mesh compression, whereas KTX2 and Meshopt are applied via post-export tooling (gltf-transform or gltfpack).

claims.statement: Blender's built-in glTF 2.0 add-on natively encodes KHR_draco_mesh_compression, while KHR_texture_basisu (KTX2) and EXT_meshopt_compression are standard Khronos extensions applied via post-export optimization tools.
claims.scope: Blender 3.6 LTS, 4.2 LTS, 5.1+ glTF-Blender-IO and Khronos glTF 2.0 extensions.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Confirmed in Blender Manual glTF 2.0 Compression section and Khronos extension specs.

blender_versions.version_notes: Native Draco encoder is bundled with Blender's official glTF 2.0 exporter across Blender 3.x-5.x. Verified against Blender 4.5.15 LTS and 5.2.3 LTS documentation (live runtime: Not Run).

records.title: glTF 2.0 Right-Handed +Y Up Coordinate System and Blender Transform Conversion
records.summary: Rules governing coordinate axis conversion between Blender (+Z Up, -Y Forward) and glTF 2.0 / Three.js (+Y Up, +Z Forward) along with TRS transform application requirements.
intent_signals: convert Blender +Z up -Y forward coordinate system to glTF 2.0 +Y up +Z forward
fix skewed rotated child hierarchy or backward facing model in Three.js
apply rotation and scale before glb export for clean TRS matrices

when_to_apply: Before exporting any asset or scene from Blender to .glb/.gltf for Three.js, React Three Fiber, Babylon.js, or PlayCanvas.
When diagnosing why an exported model faces backward, lies on its side, or has skewed child hierarchy rotations in Three.js.
when_not_to_apply: When exchanging native .blend files directly between two Blender sessions.

prerequisites: All mesh objects have Ctrl+A -> Rotation & Scale applied (Scale = 1,1,1; Rotation = 0,0,0) in Blender prior to export, and +Y Up is enabled in the glTF exporter.
principles: glTF 2.0 mandates a right-handed coordinate system where +Y is up, +Z is forward, and 1 unit equals 1 meter; Blender's exporter maps Blender -Y to glTF +Z and Blender +Z to glTF +Y when +Y Up is enabled.

glTF 2.0 nodes decompose transforms strictly into Translation, Rotation, and Scale (TRS) without shear; a rotated child under a non-uniformly scaled parent cannot be represented without skew distortion.
Semantic PascalCase or snake_case node and material names ensure @react-three/drei useGLTF and gltfjsx destructuring remain stable across iterative re-exports.

workflow_steps: Orient hero assets in Blender so the front faces -Y (Front Orthographic View, Numpad 1) and the resting base sits at Z = 0.
Apply Rotation & Scale (Ctrl+A) on all parent and child nodes so every exported node has uniform (1.0, 1.0, 1.0) scale.
Keep +Y Up enabled (default) in the Blender glTF 2.0 exporter and assign clean semantic names to all meshes and materials.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: 3D Viewport -> Viewpoint -> Front (Numpad 1); Object -> Apply -> Rotation & Scale (Ctrl+A); File -> Export -> glTF 2.0 -> Transform -> +Y Up.

observable_checks.check: Inspect Front Orthographic view (Numpad 1, looking toward +Y) in Blender before export.
observable_checks.pass_condition: The front of the asset faces the viewer in Front Orthographic view and rests on Z = 0.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: The asset appears sideways or upside-down in Front Orthographic view.

observable_checks.check: Inspect all parent nodes, Empties, and Armatures for non-uniform scale (sx != sy or sy != sz).
observable_checks.pass_condition: Every parent node has uniform (1.0, 1.0, 1.0) scale.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Non-uniform parent scale induces shear distortion on rotated child nodes during glTF TRS decomposition.

creative_affordances: Clean semantic node naming (Shoe_Upper, Sole_Mid, Lid_Pivot) turns npx gltfjsx model.glb into a self-documenting declarative React component.
Consistent Y = 0 ground origin allows swapping multiple hero .glb products inside the same <Stage> wrapper without per-asset position offsets.
known_limits: Lights exported via KHR_lights_punctual orient along -Z in local glTF node space; the Blender exporter handles this conversion automatically when +Y Up is enabled.

claims.statement: glTF 2.0 uses a right-handed coordinate system where +Y is up, +Z is forward, -X is right, and 1 unit equals 1 meter; node transforms must be decomposable into TRS (translation, rotation, scale) without skew/shear.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Confirmed in Khronos glTF 2.0 specification Section 3.4 and Section 3.2.

source_refs.locator: Section 3.4 — Coordinate System and Units; Section 3.2 — Nodes and TRS

blender_versions.version_notes: Blender glTF 2.0 exporter defaults to +Y Up enabled across Blender 3.x-5.x. Verified against Blender 4.5.15 LTS and 5.2.3 LTS documentation (live runtime: Not Run).

records.title: GLB Binary Container Structure, Export Flags, and Khronos Validator Compliance
records.summary: Specification rules for single-file .glb binary packaging (12-byte header, JSON chunk 0x4E4F534A, BIN chunk 0x004E4942), deterministic Blender export settings, and zero-error Khronos gltf-validator compliance.
intent_signals: validate glb binary header magic 0x46546C67 and 4-byte chunk alignment
configure Blender glTF 2.0 export flags Apply Modifiers UVs Normals Tangents
verify exported glb with Khronos gltf-validator zero errors before handoff

when_to_apply: When configuring Blender's glTF 2.0 exporter for production .glb delivery.
When auditing or validating an exported .glb artifact before marking it Produced or Verified.
when_not_to_apply: When intermediate multi-file .gltf + .bin inspection is temporarily needed for manual JSON diffs (convert to .glb for final delivery).

prerequisites: Export scope is explicitly filtered (Selected Objects, Visible Objects, or Active Collection) so staging and helper meshes are excluded.
principles: A valid .glb file starts with a 12-byte little-endian header (magic 0x46546C67 'glTF', version 2, total byte length), followed by a 4-byte-aligned JSON chunk (0x4E4F534A) and BIN chunk (0x004E4942).
Enabling Apply Modifiers, UVs, Normals, and Tangents during export ensures non-destructive Bevel/Weighted Normal stacks and MikkTSpace normal maps evaluate accurately in web engines.
Under law-validation-before-done, an exported .glb cannot be marked Verified without confirming file existence, non-zero byte size, valid header, and zero schema errors.

workflow_steps: Filter export scope (Include -> Selected Objects / Active Collection) and disable Cameras and Punctual Lights for standalone web props.
Select Format: glTF Binary (.glb) and enable Mesh -> Apply Modifiers, UVs, Normals, and Tangents (when normal maps are used).
Run Khronos gltf-validator or inspect the exported binary header, node/material inventory, and accessor bounds before handoff.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: File -> Export -> glTF 2.0 (.glb/.gltf); Collection Properties -> Exporters -> glTF 2.0 (Blender 4.2 LTS+).

observable_checks.check: Verify the .glb exists on disk, has byte size > 0, starts with magic 0x46546C67 ('glTF') version 2, and passes Khronos gltf-validator with 0 errors.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Binary header is valid, numErrors === 0, and all bufferViews/images resolve internally.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Missing file, truncated binary buffer, or ACCESSOR_NON_UNIT / URI_GLB_INVALID validator errors.

observable_checks.check: Inspect the exported glTF nodes and meshes list against the intended export collection.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Only intended asset nodes are present; zero Cutter_*, HighPoly_*, or Backdrop_* helper meshes leaked into the .glb.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Hidden boolean cutters or studio staging walls are present in the exported node tree.

creative_affordances: Using Blender 4.2+ Collection Exporters (Collection Properties -> Exporters -> glTF 2.0) saves deterministic export presets per collection inside the .blend file.
Single-file .glb packaging eliminates relative texture URI 404 errors when moving assets across CDN buckets.
known_limits: Vanilla Blender cannot apply modifiers during export on a mesh that simultaneously contains Shape Keys unless pre-processed.

claims.statement: A valid .glb file begins with a 12-byte header (magic = 0x46546C67, version = 2, length), followed by a 4-byte-aligned JSON chunk (0x4E4F534A) and an optional 4-byte-aligned BIN chunk (0x004E4942).
claims.scope: Khronos glTF 2.0 specification Section 4 (Binary glTF Layout).
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Exact normative binary layout in Khronos glTF 2.0 specification.

claims.statement: Blender 4.2 LTS introduced Collection Exporters (Collection Properties -> Exporters), allowing per-collection glTF 2.0 export settings and output paths to be persisted on the collection datablock.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Verified in Blender 4.2 LTS Manual — Collection Exporters.

blender_versions.version_notes: Blender 4.2 LTS+ adds persistent Collection Exporters in the Properties panel. Verified against Blender 4.5.15 LTS and 5.2.3 LTS documentation (live runtime: Not Run).

records.title: Three.js and React Three Fiber Tone Mapping, Color Management, and IBL Parity with Blender
records.summary: Rules for matching Blender's AgX/Filmic PBR appearance in Three.js (r152+ / r162+) and React Three Fiber using linear working space, AgXToneMapping or NeutralToneMapping, and HDR Environment IBL.
intent_signals: fix metallic material looking black or dark in Three.js React Three Fiber
match Blender AgX or Filmic tone mapping and color management in Three.js
configure HDR Environment IBL PMREMGenerator and SRGBColorSpace in R3F

when_to_apply: When handing off a .glb asset to a frontend Three.js or React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber / @react-three/drei) developer.
When diagnosing why a metallic or glossy .glb looks dark, washed out, or over-saturated in the browser compared to Blender.
when_not_to_apply: When rendering exclusively offline inside Blender without a web viewer target.

prerequisites: Exported .glb uses spec-compliant PBR metallic-roughness materials and modern Three.js (r152+ / r162+) is targeted.
principles: Pure conductors (Metallic = 1.0) have zero diffuse reflection and appear completely black in Three.js unless an HDR environment map (scene.environment / <Environment />) supplies specular IBL.
Three.js r152+ enables linear ColorManagement and SRGBColorSpace output by default, and r162+ provides native THREE.AgXToneMapping and Khronos THREE.NeutralToneMapping.
BaseColor and Emissive textures must use THREE.SRGBColorSpace, whereas Normal, Roughness, Metallic, and ORM maps must remain in linear THREE.NoColorSpace.

workflow_steps: Configure an HDR environment map (<Environment preset="city" /> or custom .hdr via PMREMGenerator) in the R3F/Three.js scene so metallic surfaces reflect full 360-degree lighting.
Set renderer.toneMapping to THREE.AgXToneMapping (to match Blender 4.0+ AgX) or THREE.NeutralToneMapping (for color-accurate e-commerce products) with outputColorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace.
Verify that any manually loaded Normal/ORM textures keep THREE.NoColorSpace while BaseColor/Emissive textures use THREE.SRGBColorSpace.
implementation_guidance.blender_context: Render Properties -> Color Management (View Transform: AgX); World Properties -> Environment Texture (HDRI); Three.js Canvas / WebGLRenderer config.

observable_checks.check: Verify the R3F/Three.js viewer specification includes scene.environment (<Environment /> or PMREMGenerator).
observable_checks.pass_condition: Metallic and glossy materials receive full 360-degree specular reflection from an HDR environment map.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Metallic surfaces look black or flat grey because only punctual lights are active.

observable_checks.check: Verify the handoff document specifies the target tone mapping (AgX, ACESFilmic, or Neutral) and SRGBColorSpace output.
observable_checks.pass_condition: Frontend viewer configuration matches the Blender look-dev view transform.
observable_checks.fail_indicator: Viewer defaults to NoToneMapping or mismatched exposure, blowing out specular highlights.

creative_affordances: Using @react-three/drei <Lightformer> inside <Environment resolution={512}> recreates procedural studio softboxes directly in the browser's PMREM environment map.
Khronos THREE.NeutralToneMapping guarantees that a sneaker or cosmetic bottle's brand color matches the CSS page palette.
known_limits: Real-time WebGL transmission (MeshPhysicalMaterial transmission: 1) approximates single-bounce refraction rather than Cycles multi-bounce path-traced caustics.

claims.statement: Three.js r152 enabled linear ColorManagement and SRGBColorSpace output by default, and subsequent releases added AgXToneMapping and Khronos NeutralToneMapping for PBR parity.
claims.uncertainty_or_version_note: Confirmed in official Three.js Color Management documentation.

source_refs.locator: Khronos PBR Neutral Tone Mapper & Viewer Parity

blender_versions.version_notes: Blender 4.0+ AgX view transform pairs directly with THREE.AgXToneMapping in Three.js. Verified against Blender 4.5.15 LTS and 5.2.3 LTS documentation (live runtime: Not Run).
